translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 292
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 292

sentences.zh: 【後周紀三】 起閼逢攝提格五月，盡柔兆執徐二月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Zhou Annals 3] Beginning in the fifth month of the year Quefeng Shedige, extending through the second month of the year Rouzhao Zhixu, altogether a little more than one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Zhou Annals 3] Covering from the fifth month of 954 through the second month of 956, a span of slightly more than one year.

sentences.zh: 太祖聖神恭肅文武孝皇帝下顯德元年（

translations.literal: Below: the Sagely, Divine, Reverent, Solemn, Civil, and Martial Filial Emperor Taizu, first year of Xiande (
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Shizong — Xiande, year 1 (

sentences.zh: 甲寅，公元九五四年）

translations.literal: Jiayin, corresponding to the year 954 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: CE, cyclical year Jiayin)

sentences.zh: 五月，甲戌朔，王逵自潭州遷於朗州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day of the cycle (day Jiaxu), Wang Kui moved his base from Tanzhou to Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the new moon of day Jiaxu, Wang Kui transferred from Tanzhou to Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 以周行逢知潭州事，以潘叔嗣為岳州團練使。

translations.literal: Zhou Xingfeng was appointed to administer Tanzhou affairs, and Pan Shusi was made military commissioner of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingfeng was put in charge of Tanzhou, and Pan Shusi was appointed regimental commissioner of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 丙子，帝至晉陽城下，旗幟環城四十里。

translations.literal: On day Bingzi, the Emperor reached beneath the walls of Jinyang; banners and standards ringed the city for forty li.
translations.idiomatic: On day Bingzi, the emperor arrived below Jinyang; his standards encircled the city for forty li.

sentences.zh: 楊兗疑北漢代州防禦使鄭處謙貳於周，召與計事，欲圖之。

translations.literal: Yang Gun suspected that Zheng Chuqian, defense commissioner of Daizhou for Northern Han, was wavering toward Zhou, and summoned him to consult on affairs, intending to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gun suspected that Northern Han's Daizhou defense commissioner Zheng Chuqian was leaning toward the Zhou, so he summoned him to discuss plans with the intent of doing away with him.

sentences.zh: 處謙知之，不往。

translations.literal: Chuqian learned of this and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Chuqian learned of the plot and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 兗使胡騎數十守其城門，處謙殺之，因閉門拒兗。

translations.literal: Gun sent several dozen Khitan horsemen to guard the city gates; Chuqian killed them and then shut the gates to resist Gun.
translations.idiomatic: Gun posted several dozen Khitan cavalry at the gates; Chuqian killed them, shut the gates, and barred Gun from the city.

sentences.zh: 兗奔歸契丹。

translations.literal: Gun fled back to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Gun fled back to the Khitan court.

sentences.zh: 契丹主怒其無功，囚之。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler, angry at his lack of achievement, imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor, furious at his failure, had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 處謙舉城來降。

translations.literal: Chuqian surrendered the entire city.
translations.idiomatic: Chuqian surrendered the whole city to the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，置靜塞軍於代州，以鄭處謙為節度使。

translations.literal: On day Dingchou, the Jingse Army was established at Daizhou, with Zheng Chuqian as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On day Dingchou, the Jingse Army was set up at Daizhou, and Zheng Chuqian was made its military governor.

sentences.zh: 契丹數千騎屯忻、代之間，為北漢之援，庚辰，遣符彥卿等將步騎萬餘擊之。

translations.literal: Several thousand Khitan horsemen were encamped between Xin and Dai as reinforcements for Northern Han; on day Gengchen, Fu Yanqing and others were sent leading more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Khitan horsemen lay between Xinzhou and Daizhou in support of Northern Han; on day Gengchen, the court dispatched Fu Yanqing and others at the head of over ten thousand foot and horse to strike them.

sentences.zh: 彥卿入忻州，契丹退保忻口。

translations.literal: Yanqing entered Xinzhou; the Khitan withdrew to hold Xin Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing marched into Xinzhou, and the Khitan fell back to defend Xin Pass.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，置寧化軍於汾州，以石、沁二州隸之。

translations.literal: On day Dinghai, the Ninghua Army was established at Fenzhou, with Shi and Qin prefectures placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: On day Dinghai, the Ninghua Army was created at Fenzhou, with the prefectures of Shi and Qin subordinated to it.

sentences.zh: 代州將桑珪、解文遇殺鄭處謙，誣奏雲潛通契丹。

translations.literal: The Daizhou generals Sang Gui and Xie Wenyü killed Zheng Chuqian and falsely memorialized that Yun had secretly communicated with the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Daizhou generals Sang Gui and Xie Wenyü assassinated Zheng Chuqian and falsely reported that Yun was in secret contact with the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 符彥卿奏請益兵，癸巳，遣李筠、張永德將兵三千赴之。

translations.literal: Fu Yanqing memorialized requesting additional troops; on day Guisi, Li Yun and Zhang Yongde were sent leading three thousand soldiers to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing asked for reinforcements; on day Guisi, Li Yun and Zhang Yongde were sent with three thousand men to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 契丹游騎時至忻州城下，丙申，彥卿與諸將陳以待之。

translations.literal: Khitan raiding horsemen frequently came to beneath the walls of Xinzhou; on day Bingshen, Yanqing and the generals drew up in formation to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan scouting cavalry kept appearing below Xinzhou; on day Bingshen, Yanqing and his officers formed battle lines to receive them.

sentences.zh: 史彥超將二十騎為前鋒，遇契丹，與戰，李筠引兵繼之，殺契丹二千人。

translations.literal: Shi Yanchao led twenty horsemen as vanguard, encountered the Khitan, and fought; Li Yun brought troops up in support and killed two thousand Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanchao took twenty horsemen as the vanguard, clashed with the Khitan, and Li Yun came up with the main body; together they killed two thousand Khitan.

sentences.zh: 彥超恃勇輕進，去大軍浸遠，眾寡不敵，為契丹所殺，筠僅以身免，周兵死傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Yanchao, relying on his bravery, advanced lightly and drew gradually farther from the main army; outnumbered, he was killed by the Khitan, and Yun barely escaped with his life; Zhou troops died and were wounded in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao, overconfident in his valor, pressed ahead until he was far from the main force; outnumbered, he was slain by the Khitan. Yun barely escaped, and Zhou losses were heavy.

sentences.zh: 彥卿退保忻州，尋引兵還晉陽。

translations.literal: Yanqing withdrew to defend Xinzhou and soon led his troops back to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing fell back to hold Xinzhou and soon returned with his army to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 府州防禦使折德扆將州兵來朝。

translations.literal: Zhe Deyi, defense commissioner of Fuzhou, led the prefectural troops to court.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou defense commissioner Zhe Deyi brought his prefectural troops to present themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，復置永安軍於府州，以德扆為節度使。

translations.literal: On day Xinchou, the Yong'an Army was re-established at Fuzhou, with Deyi as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On day Xinchou, the Yong'an Army was restored at Fuzhou, and Deyi was appointed its military governor.

sentences.zh: 時大發兵夫，東自懷、孟，西及薄、陝，以攻晉陽，不克。

translations.literal: At this time corvée laborers were mobilized on a large scale, from Huai and Meng in the east to Bo and Shan in the west, to attack Jinyang, but they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The court had mobilized vast numbers of laborers from Huai and Meng in the east to Bo and Shan in the west for the assault on Jinyang, yet the city would not fall.

sentences.zh: 會久雨，士卒疲病，及史彥超死，乃議引還。

translations.literal: It happened that prolonged rain fell, the soldiers grew weary and ill, and when Shi Yanchao died, they deliberated on withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged rains set in, the troops fell ill with exhaustion, and after Shi Yanchao's death the command began to discuss withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 初，王得中返自契丹，值周兵圍晉陽，留止代州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Dezong had returned from the Khitan; he happened upon Zhou troops besieging Jinyang and remained at Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Dezong had returned from the Khitan court and, finding Zhou forces besieging Jinyang, stayed at Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 及桑珪殺鄭處謙，囚得中，送於周軍。

translations.literal: When Sang Gui killed Zheng Chuqian, he imprisoned Dezong and sent him to the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: When Sang Gui killed Zheng Chuqian, he seized Dezong and handed him over to the Zhou army.

sentences.zh: 帝釋之，賜以帶、馬，問，「虜兵何時當至？」

translations.literal: The Emperor released him, bestowed a belt and horse upon him, and asked, "When will the barbarian troops arrive?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor freed him, gave him a belt and horse, and asked, "When will the enemy forces arrive?"

sentences.zh: 得中曰：「臣受命送楊袞，他無所求。」

translations.literal: Dezong said: "Your subject received orders to escort Yang Gun; beyond that I have no other knowledge."
translations.idiomatic: Dezong replied, "I was charged only with escorting Yang Gun back; I know nothing beyond that."

sentences.zh: 或謂得中曰：「契丹許公發兵，公不以實告，契丹兵即至，公得無危乎？」

translations.literal: Someone said to Dezong: "The Khitan promised you they would send troops; if you do not report this truthfully, when Khitan troops arrive will you not be in danger?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Dezong, "The Khitan promised you they would raise an army. If you do not tell the truth, their troops will come—and will you not be in peril?"

sentences.zh: 得中太息曰：「吾食劉氏祿，有老母在圍中，若以實告，周人必發兵據險以拒之。

translations.literal: Dezong sighed deeply and said: "I have eaten the Liu family's salary; my aged mother is within the besieged city. If I report truthfully, the Zhou will surely send troops to seize the passes and resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong sighed and said, "I have drawn salary from the house of Liu; my old mother is inside the besieged city. If I told the truth, the Zhou would surely send troops to hold the passes and block them.

sentences.zh: 如此，家國兩亡，吾獨生何益！

translations.literal: In that case, both family and state would perish—what good would my living alone do!
translations.idiomatic: Then both my family and my state would be destroyed—what good would it do for me alone to survive!

sentences.zh: 不若殺身以全家國，所得多矣！」

translations.literal: Better to give up my life to preserve family and state—the gain would be far greater!"
translations.idiomatic: Better to die and save them both—that would be the greater gain!"

sentences.zh: 甲辰，帝以得中欺罔，縊殺之。

translations.literal: On day Jiachen, the Emperor, on the grounds that Dezong had deceived him, had him strangled.
translations.idiomatic: On day Jiachen, the emperor judged that Dezong had deceived him and had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，帝發晉陽。

translations.literal: On day Yisi, the Emperor departed from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On day Yisi, the emperor marched out from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 匡國節度使藥元福言於帝曰：「進軍易，退軍難。」

translations.literal: Yao Yuanfu, military governor of Kuangguo, said to the Emperor: "Advancing the army is easy; withdrawing the army is hard."
translations.idiomatic: Kuangguo military governor Yao Yuanfu told the emperor, "It is easy to advance an army but hard to withdraw one."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕一以委卿。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I entrust this entirely to you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I leave it entirely to you."

sentences.zh: 元福乃勒兵成列而殿。

translations.literal: Yuanfu then drew up the troops in formation to serve as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu then formed the troops into ranks to cover the rear.

sentences.zh: 北漢果出兵追躡，元福擊走之。

translations.literal: Northern Han did indeed send troops in pursuit; Yuanfu struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Han did send troops in pursuit, and Yuanfu beat them back.

sentences.zh: 然軍還匆遽，芻糧數十萬在城下者，悉焚棄之。

translations.literal: Yet the army returned in haste; several hundred thousand units of fodder and grain left below the city were all burned and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the withdrawal was rushed, and several hundred thousand loads of fodder and grain stockpiled below the walls were burned and abandoned.

sentences.zh: 軍中訛言相驚，或相剽掠，軍須失亡不可勝計。

translations.literal: False rumors alarmed one another within the army; some plundered one another; military supplies lost and destroyed were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread panic through the ranks, some men robbed one another, and military stores lost were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 所得北漢州縣，周所置刺史等皆棄城走，惟代州桑珪既叛北漢，又不敢歸周，嬰城自守，北漢遣兵攻拔之。

translations.literal: Of the Northern Han prefectures and counties that had been taken, the prefects and others appointed by Zhou all abandoned their cities and fled; only Sang Gui of Daizhou, having rebelled against Northern Han yet not daring to return to Zhou, closed the city and held it alone, until Northern Han sent troops to attack and capture it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Northern Han prefectures and counties the Zhou had taken, the Zhou-appointed prefects and officials all fled their posts. Only Sang Gui at Daizhou, having turned against Northern Han but not daring to submit to the Zhou, held the city under siege until Northern Han sent troops and retook it.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，帝至潞州。

translations.literal: On day Yiyou, the Emperor reached Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On day Yiyou, the emperor arrived at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲子，至鄭州。

translations.literal: On day Jiazi, he reached Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On day Jiazi, he reached Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，謁嵩陵。

translations.literal: On day Bingyin, he visited Songling.
translations.idiomatic: On day Bingyin, he paid his respects at Songling.

sentences.zh: 庚午，至大梁。

translations.literal: On day Gengwu, he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On day Gengwu, he entered Daliang.

sentences.zh: 帝違眾議破北漢，自是政事無大小皆親決，百官受成於上而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor, against the consensus, had attacked Northern Han; from this time onward affairs great and small were all decided by him in person, and the hundred officials merely received completed decisions from above.
translations.idiomatic: Having overruled his advisers to strike Northern Han, the emperor from then on decided every matter of state himself, great or small, while officials merely received his finished decisions.

sentences.zh: 河南府推官高錫上書諫，以為：「四海之廣，萬機之眾，雖堯舜不能獨治，必擇人而任之。

translations.literal: Gao Xi, investigating censor of Henan prefecture, submitted a memorial of remonstrance, stating: "The realm is vast and affairs innumerable; even Yao and Shun could not govern alone—they had to select men and entrust them.
translations.idiomatic: Henan prefecture investigating censor Gao Xi submitted a memorial arguing that even Yao and Shun could not govern the vast realm and its countless affairs alone—they had to choose the right men and delegate to them.

sentences.zh: 今陛下一以身親之，天下不謂陛下聰明睿智足以兼百官之任，皆言陛下褊迫疑忌舉不信群臣也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty personally handles everything alone; the realm will not say that Your Majesty is so intelligent and wise as to be able to combine the duties of the hundred officials—all will say that Your Majesty is narrow, urgent, suspicious, and jealous, and does not trust the ministers at all.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty now handles everything in person, the realm will not take this as proof of wisdom sufficient to discharge every official's duty; men will say instead that Your Majesty is narrow-minded, anxious, and suspicious, trusting no minister at all.

sentences.zh: 不若選能知人公正者以為宰相，能愛民聽訟者以為守令，能豐財足食者使掌金谷，能原情守法者使掌刑獄，陛下但垂拱明堂，視其功過而賞罰之，天下何憂不治！

translations.literal: Better to select men able to know people and be fair as chancellors, men able to love the people and hear lawsuits as prefects and magistrates, men able to enrich finances and fill granaries to manage revenue and grain, men able to trace circumstances and uphold law to manage prisons—Your Majesty need only sit at ease in the Bright Hall, observe their merits and faults, and reward and punish them; what worry would there be that the realm would not be well governed!
translations.idiomatic: Appoint as chancellor one who knows men and judges fairly; as prefects and magistrates those who love the people and hear cases well; put revenue and grain in the hands of those who can enrich the treasury and fill the stores; put justice in the hands of those who weigh circumstances and uphold the law—then Your Majesty need only sit at ease in the Bright Hall, watch their merits and faults, and reward or punish accordingly. What fear is there that the realm will not be well governed?

sentences.zh: 何必降君尊而代臣職，屈貴位而親賤事，無乃失為政之本乎！」

translations.literal: Why must you lower the ruler's dignity to replace ministers' duties, bend exalted rank to attend to mean affairs—is this not losing the root of governing!"
translations.idiomatic: Why lower the dignity of the throne to do ministers' work, or bend exalted rank to petty tasks—does that not abandon the very foundation of rule?"

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 錫，河中人也。

translations.literal: "Xi was a man of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: "Xi was a native of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 北漢主憂憤成疾，悉以國事委其子侍衛都指揮使承鈞。

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler, through worry and indignation, fell ill; he entrusted all state affairs to his son, the commander of the palace guards, Cheng Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Han ruler fell ill with worry and resentment and entrusted all affairs of state to his son Cheng Jun, commander of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 河西節度使申師厚不俟詔，擅棄鎮入朝，署其子為留後。

translations.literal: Shen Shihou, military governor of Hexi, without awaiting an edict on his own authority abandoned his post and entered court, appointing his son as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi military governor Shen Shihou, without awaiting orders, abandoned his command and came to court, leaving his son as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸酉朔，責授率府副率。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day of the cycle (day Guiyou), he was demoted by imperial reprimand to vice-commandant of the Rate Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the new moon of day Guiyou, he was demoted to vice-commandant of the Rate Office.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，加吳越王錢弘俶天下兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: On day Dingchou, Qian Hongchu, King of Wuyue, was promoted to commander-in-chief of all armies under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On day Dingchou, Wuyue king Qian Hongchu was promoted to commander-in-chief of all armies under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，加門下侍郎、同平章事范質守司徒，以樞密直學士、工部侍郎長山景范為中書侍郎、同平章事、判三司。

translations.literal: On day Guisi, Fan Zhi, vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal councilor, was promoted to Defender of the Situ; Jing Fan of Changshan, academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and vice minister of Works, was made vice director of the Secretariat, co-equal councilor, and overseer of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: On day Guisi, Fan Zhi, vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal councilor, was made Defender of the Situ; Jing Fan of Changshan, bureau academician and vice minister of Works, was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, co-equal councilor, and overseer of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 加樞密使、同平章事鄭仁誨兼侍中。

translations.literal: Zheng Renhui, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and co-equal councilor, was additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau commissioner and co-equal councilor Zheng Renhui was also made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以樞密副使魏仁浦為樞密使。

translations.literal: On day Yiwei, Wei Renpu, vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On day Yiwei, bureau vice commissioner Wei Renpu was promoted to commissioner.

sentences.zh: 范質既為司徒，司徒竇貞固歸洛陽，府縣以民視之，課役皆不免。

translations.literal: Once Fan Zhi had become Situ, Dou Zhengu, the former Situ, returned to Luoyang; the prefecture and counties treated him as a commoner, and levies and corvée were not waived.
translations.idiomatic: After Fan Zhi received the title of Situ, the former holder Dou Zhengu returned to Luoyang; local officials treated him as an ordinary subject, and he remained liable for taxes and labor service.

sentences.zh: 貞固訴於留守向訓，訓不聽。

translations.literal: Zhengu appealed to the regent Xiang Xun, but Xun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengu appealed to Luoyang regent Xiang Xun, who refused to intervene.

sentences.zh: 初，帝與北漢主相拒於高平，命前澤州刺史李彥崇將兵守江豬嶺，遏北漢主歸路。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor and the Northern Han ruler confronted each other at Gaoping, he had ordered the former prefect of Zezhou, Li Yanchong, to lead troops to hold Jiangzhu Ridge and block the Northern Han ruler's route of return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor and the Northern Han ruler faced each other at Gaoping, he had ordered former Zezhou prefect Li Yanchong to hold Jiangzhu Ridge and cut off the Northern Han ruler's line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 彥崇聞樊愛能等南遁，引兵退，北漢主果自其路遁去。

translations.literal: Yanchong heard that Fan Aineng and others had fled south and withdrew his troops; the Northern Han ruler did indeed escape by that route.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchong heard that Fan Aineng and others had broken south in flight and pulled his men back; the Northern Han ruler escaped by that very route.

sentences.zh: 八月，己酉，貶彥崇率府副率。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day Jiyou, Yanchong was demoted to vice-commandant of the Rate Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on day Jiyou, Yanchong was demoted to vice-commandant of the Rate Office.

sentences.zh: 己巳，廢鎮國軍。

translations.literal: On day Jisi, the Zhenguo Army was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On day Jisi, the Zhenguo Army was abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖以建雄節度使王晏有拒北漢之功，其鄉里有滕縣，徙晏為武寧節度使。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Wang Yan, military governor of Jianxiong, had the merit of resisting Northern Han and his home district had Teng County, Taizu transferred Yan to be military governor of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Jianxiong military governor Wang Yan had distinguished himself against Northern Han and his home district included Teng County, Taizu transferred him to Wuning.

sentences.zh: 晏少時嘗為群盜，至鎮，悉召故黨，贈之金帛、鞍馬，謂曰：「吾鄉素名多盜，昔吾與諸君皆嘗為之，想後來者無能居諸君之右。

translations.literal: Yan in his youth had been a bandit leader; upon reaching his post he summoned all his old companions, bestowed gold, silks, saddles, and horses on them, and said: "My district has long been famed for many bandits; in the past I and you gentlemen all did this—I expect no newcomers can surpass you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had been a bandit in his youth; on taking up his post he summoned all his old comrades, gave them gold, silks, saddles, and horses, and said, "Our district has long been notorious for bandits. You and I were among them once, and I doubt any newcomer could match you.

sentences.zh: 諸君幸為我語之，使勿復為，為者吾必族之。」

translations.literal: I ask you gentlemen kindly to speak to them for me and tell them not to do it again—whoever does, I shall exterminate his clan."
translations.idiomatic: Please pass the word for me: let them not take it up again, for I will exterminate the clan of anyone who does."

sentences.zh: 於是一境清肅。

translations.literal: Thereupon the entire jurisdiction was cleared and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The whole region was soon pacified.

sentences.zh: 九月，徐州人請為之立衣錦碑。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the people of Xuzhou requested that a "Returning in Brocade" stele be erected for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the people of Xuzhou asked to erect for him a "Returning in Brocade" memorial stele.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲辰，左羽林大將軍孟漢卿坐納蒿稅，場官擾民，多取耗餘，賜死。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on day Jiachen, Meng Hanqing, great general of the Left Feathered Forest, was sentenced to death for accepting rush-tax payments: the field officials harassed the people and took excessive surplus.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on day Jiachen, Left Feathered Forest great general Meng Hanqing was sentenced to death for taking rush-tax payments while his field officers harassed the people and exacted excessive surcharges.

sentences.zh: 有司奏漢卿罪不至死。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized that Hanqing's crime did not warrant death.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices reported that Hanqing's offense did not merit death.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕知之，欲以懲眾耳！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I know it—I wish to warn the multitude, that is all!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I know—but I mean to make an example of him!"

sentences.zh: 己酉，廢安遠、永清軍。

translations.literal: On day Jiyou, the Anyuan and Yongqing armies were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On day Jiyou, the Anyuan and Yongqing armies were abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，宿衛之士，累朝相承，務求姑息，不欲簡閱，恐傷人情，由是羸老者居多。

translations.literal: Earlier, the palace guard soldiers, handed down through successive reigns, strove for indulgence and did not wish to be inspected, fearing to hurt feelings; thus the weak and aged were mostly numerous.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the palace guards had been managed with indulgence: no one wanted to inspect them for fear of giving offense, and so the ranks were filled with the weak and the old.

sentences.zh: 但驕蹇不用命，實不可用，每遇大敵，不走即降。

translations.literal: They were only arrogant and obstinate, disobedient to orders, and in truth unusable; whenever they met a strong enemy, if they did not flee they surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: They were arrogant and insubordinate, useless in practice: whenever they met a serious enemy they either fled or surrendered.

sentences.zh: 其所以失國，亦多由此。

translations.literal: That states lost their realms was also largely due to this.
translations.idiomatic: Many a dynasty had lost its realm for just this reason.

sentences.zh: 帝因高平之戰，始知其弊。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because of the battle of Gaoping, first learned of this defect.
translations.idiomatic: The battle of Gaoping taught the emperor how deep the problem ran.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，謂侍臣曰：「凡兵務精不務多，今以農夫百未能養甲士一，奈何浚民之膏澤，養此無用之物乎！

translations.literal: On day Guihai, he said to his attending ministers: "In all military affairs, quality is sought, not quantity; now a hundred farmers can scarcely support one armored soldier—how can we drain the people's fat and grease to maintain these useless things!
translations.idiomatic: On day Guihai he told his ministers, "In war, quality matters, not numbers. A hundred farmers can barely support one armored soldier—why drain the people's substance to feed these useless men?

sentences.zh: 且健懦不分，眾何所勸！」

translations.literal: Moreover, if the strong and weak are not distinguished, what will the multitude be encouraged toward!"
translations.idiomatic: And if the fit and the feeble are not separated, what incentive is there for anyone to excel?"

sentences.zh: 乃命大簡諸軍，精銳者升之上軍，羸者斥去之。

translations.literal: He then ordered a great inspection of all armies: the elite and sharp were promoted to the upper army, the weak were expelled.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a thorough review of all armies: the elite were promoted to the upper corps, the weak were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又以驍勇之士多為諸籓鎮所蓄，詔募天下壯士，咸遣詣闕，命太祖皇帝選其尤者為殿前諸班，其騎步諸軍，各命將帥選之。

translations.literal: Moreover, because many valiant warriors were kept by the various frontier commands, he decreed recruiting stalwart men throughout the realm, all to be sent to court, and ordered the Taizu Emperor to select the finest for the palace guard companies; for the cavalry and infantry armies, each commander was ordered to select them.
translations.idiomatic: Because many of the bravest men were hoarded by the regional commands, he decreed a nationwide levy of stalwarts to be sent to court, where Taizu was to pick the best for the palace guard companies while each army commander selected men for his own cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 由是士卒精強，近代無比，征伐四方，所向皆捷，選練之力也。

translations.literal: From this the soldiers became elite and strong, unmatched in recent times; campaigns in the four directions met success wherever they went—the power of selection and training.
translations.idiomatic: The troops became the finest seen in generations; in every campaign they carried the day. This was the fruit of rigorous selection and training.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，帝謂侍臣曰：「諸道盜賊頗多，討捕終不能絕，蓋由累朝分命使臣巡檢，致籓侯、守令皆不致力。

translations.literal: On day Wuchen, the Emperor said to his attending ministers: "Bandits in the various circuits are quite numerous; suppression and capture never end them—this is largely because successive reigns dispatched commissioners to conduct inspections, causing the frontier lords, prefects, and magistrates all not to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: On day Wuchen the emperor told his ministers, "Banditry is rife in the circuits and never seems to end, largely because past reigns sent touring inspectors, so the regional lords, prefects, and magistrates never threw themselves into the work.

sentences.zh: 宜悉召還，專委節鎮、州縣，責其清肅。」

translations.literal: They should all be recalled, and responsibility entrusted solely to the military governors, prefectures, and counties, charging them with clearing and pacifying."
translations.idiomatic: Recall them all and leave the work solely to the military governors and local officials, holding them responsible for restoring order."

sentences.zh: 河自楊劉至於博州百二十里，連年東潰，分為二派，匯為大澤，瀰漫數百里。

translations.literal: The Yellow River from Yangliu to Bozhou, one hundred twenty li, for successive years breached eastward, divided into two branches, and pooled into a great marsh, spreading across several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: For a hundred twenty li from Yangliu to Bozhou the Yellow River had breached eastward year after year, splitting into two channels and spreading into a vast marsh hundreds of li across.

sentences.zh: 又東北壞古堤而出，灌齊、棣、淄諸州，至於海涯，漂沒民田廬不可勝計，流民采菰稗、捕魚以給食，朝廷屢遣使者不能塞。

translations.literal: It again broke the ancient dike to the northeast and poured out, inundating Qi, Di, and Zi prefectures as far as the seashore; civilian fields and dwellings washed away were beyond counting; displaced people gathered wild rice and mallow and caught fish for food; the court repeatedly sent envoys but could not block it.
translations.idiomatic: It then burst the old dike to the northeast and flooded Qi, Di, and Zi prefectures all the way to the coast, drowning fields and homes beyond reckoning. Refugees lived on wild grains and fish, and repeated imperial missions failed to staunch the breach.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊戌，帝遣李穀詣澶、鄆、齊按視堤塞，役徒六萬，三十日而畢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on day Wuxu, the Emperor sent Li Gu to Yan, Yun, and Qi to inspect dikes and blockages; six hundred thousand laborers were employed, and the work was completed in thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on day Wuxu, the emperor sent Li Gu to inspect the dikes of Yan, Yun, and Qi; sixty thousand laborers finished the repairs in thirty days.

sentences.zh: 北漢主疾病，命其子承鈞監國，尋殂。

translations.literal: The Northern Han ruler fell ill, ordered his son Cheng Jun to oversee the state, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Han ruler fell ill, put his son Cheng Jun in charge of state affairs, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 遣使告哀於契丹。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to announce the mourning to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to announce his death to the Khitan court.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣驃騎大將軍、知內侍省事劉承訓冊命承鈞為帝，更名鈞。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent the swift-cavalry great general and director of the Inner Palace Service, Liu Cheng Xun, to invest Cheng Jun as emperor and rename him Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan dispatched swift-cavalry great general Liu Cheng Xun, director of the Inner Palace Service, to invest Cheng Jun as emperor and rename him Jun.

sentences.zh: 北漢孝和帝性孝謹，既嗣位，勤於為政，愛民禮士，境內粗安。

translations.literal: The Northern Han Emperor Xiaohé was by nature filial and cautious; once he succeeded to the throne, he was diligent in governing, loved the people and honored scholars, and within his borders there was rough peace.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Han's Emperor Xiaohé was filial and prudent by nature; once enthroned he applied himself to government, cared for the people, honored scholars, and brought a measure of peace within his borders.

sentences.zh: 每上表於契丹主稱男，契丹主賜之詔，謂之「兒皇帝」。

translations.literal: Whenever he submitted a memorial to the Khitan ruler he styled himself "son"; the Khitan ruler bestowed edicts upon him, calling him the "Son Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: In every memorial to the Khitan ruler he styled himself the Khitan's "son"; the Khitan addressed him in edicts as the "Son Emperor."

sentences.zh: 馬希萼之帥群蠻破長沙也，府庫累世之積，皆為漵州蠻酋苻彥通所掠，彥通由是富強，稱王於溪洞間。

translations.literal: When Ma Xie led the various Man tribes to break Changsha, the accumulations of the treasury over generations were all plundered by Fu Yantong, Man chieftain of Xuzhou; Yantong thereby became rich and strong and styled himself king among the stream grottoes.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Xie led the tribal forces that sacked Changsha, the treasury's hoard of generations fell to Xuzhou Man chieftain Fu Yantong, who grew rich and powerful enough to proclaim himself king among the hill country.

sentences.zh: 王逵既得湖南，欲遣使撫之，募能往者，其將王虔朗請行。

translations.literal: Once Wang Kui had taken Hunan, he wished to send envoys to pacify it, recruited men able to go, and his officer Wang Qianlang requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Kui secured Hunan, he sought envoys to pacify the region; his officer Wang Qianlang volunteered.

sentences.zh: 既至，彥通盛侍衛而見之，禮貌甚倨。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Yantong received him with a grand guard escort and was very arrogant in his courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival, Yantong received him with an imposing guard and treated him with studied arrogance.

sentences.zh: 虔朗厲聲責之曰：「足下自稱苻秦苒裔，宜知禮義，有以異於群蠻。

translations.literal: Qianlang sternly rebuked him, saying: "You style yourself a descendant of Fu Qin's Ran clan—you ought to know ritual and righteousness and be different from the various Man tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlang rebuked him sharply: "You claim descent from the house of Fu Qin—you ought to know ritual and propriety and stand apart from the hill tribes.

sentences.zh: 昔馬氏在湖南，足下祖父皆北面事之。

translations.literal: In the past when the Ma clan ruled Hunan, your grandfather and father all faced north to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ma clan held Hunan, your grandfather and father both bowed north to serve them.

sentences.zh: 今王公盡得馬氏之地，足下不早往乞盟，致使者先來，又不接之以禮，異日得無悔乎！」

translations.literal: Now the prince has taken all the Ma lands; you did not go early to beg alliance, yet when the envoy came first you did not receive him with courtesy—will you not regret this someday!"
translations.idiomatic: Now Lord Wang holds all that the Ma once possessed. You did not come early to seek alliance; when his envoy arrived first, you failed to receive him properly—will you not regret this one day?"

sentences.zh: 彥通慚懼，起，執虔朗手謝之。

translations.literal: Yantong, ashamed and afraid, rose and took Qianlang's hand in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Yantong, ashamed and alarmed, rose and took Qianlang's hand in apology.

sentences.zh: 虔朗知其可動，因說之曰：「溪洞之地，隋、唐之世皆為州縣，著在圖籍。

translations.literal: Qianlang knew he could be moved and therefore persuaded him, saying: "The stream-grotto lands in Sui and Tang times were all prefectures and counties, recorded in the maps and registers.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Yantong could be swayed, Qianlang urged him on: "In Sui and Tang times these stream lands were regular prefectures and counties, entered in the official registers.

sentences.zh: 今足下上無天子之詔，下無使府之命，雖自王於山谷之間，不過蠻夷一酋長耳！

translations.literal: Now you have above no Son of Heaven's edict, below no commissionerate's order—though you style yourself king among the valleys, you are no more than a single chieftain of the Man and Yi!
translations.idiomatic: You hold no imperial edict from above and no commissioner's order from below; though you call yourself king in the hills, you are no more than a tribal chieftain!

sentences.zh: 曷若去王號，自歸於王公，王公必以天子之命授足下節度使，與中國侯伯等夷，豈不尊榮哉！」

translations.literal: How much better to cast off the title of king and submit to the prince yourself—the prince will surely invest you as military governor by the Son of Heaven's command, equal to the marquises and earls of the Central Realm—would that not be honor and glory!"
translations.idiomatic: Better to drop your royal title and submit to Lord Wang, who will surely have the Son of Heaven appoint you military governor, your rank equal to the great lords of the realm—what honor could surpass that?"

sentences.zh: 彥通大喜，即日去王號，因虔朗獻銅鼓數枚於王逵。

translations.literal: Yantong was greatly pleased, that very day cast off his royal title, and through Qianlang presented several bronze drums to Wang Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Yantong was delighted, renounced his royal title that same day, and sent several bronze drums to Wang Kui through Qianlang.

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「虔朗一言勝數萬兵，真國士也！」

translations.literal: Kui said: "One word from Qianlang is worth tens of thousands of soldiers—truly a man of the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "One speech from Qianlang is worth tens of thousands of troops—a true pillar of the realm!"

sentences.zh: 承製以彥通為黔中節度使，以虔朗為都指揮使，預聞府政。

translations.literal: By imperial order Yantong was made military governor of Qianzhong, and Qianlang was made commander-in-chief with a voice in prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order Yantong was made military governor of Qianzhong, and Qianlang commander-in-chief with a voice in prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 虔朗，桂州人也。

translations.literal: Qianlang was a man of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlang was a native of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 逵慮西界鎮遏使、錦州刺史劉瑫為邊患，表為鎮南節度副使，充西界都招討使。

translations.literal: Kui, fearing that Liu Tan, frontier suppression commissioner and prefect of Jinzhou, might become a border threat, memorialized making him vice military governor of Zhennan and overall frontier commander of the western border.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that frontier commissioner and Jinzhou prefect Liu Tan might become a border menace, Kui had him appointed vice military governor of Zhennan and overall commander of the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 是歲，湖南大饑，民食草木實。

translations.literal: That year Hunan suffered great famine; the people ate the fruit of trees and grasses.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hunan suffered severe famine, and the people lived on wild plants and tree fruit.

sentences.zh: 武清節度使、知潭州事周行逢開倉以賑之，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Zhou Xingfeng, military governor of Wuqing and administrator of Tanzhou affairs, opened the granaries to relieve them and preserved very many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Wuqing military governor and Tanzhou administrator Zhou Xingfeng opened the granaries for relief and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 行逢起於微賤，知民間疾苦，勵精為治，嚴而無私，辟署僚屬，皆取廉介之士，約束簡要，吏民便之，其自奉甚薄；

translations.literal: Xingfeng rose from humble origins, knew the people's hardships, strove in spirit to govern, was strict yet unselfish, appointed subordinates all chosen from upright and incorruptible men, regulations were simple and concise, officials and people found it convenient, and his own maintenance was very meager;
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng had risen from humble origins, knew the people's hardships, and governed with tireless zeal—strict yet impartial. He appointed only upright men, kept regulations simple, and made government easy for officials and commoners alike, while living himself on very little;

sentences.zh: 或譏其太儉，行逢曰：「馬氏父子窮奢極靡，不恤百姓，今子孫乞食於人，又足效乎！」

translations.literal: some mocked him for being too frugal; Xingfeng said: "The Ma father and son exhausted luxury to the extreme and did not pity the people—now their descendants beg food from others; is that worth imitating!"
translations.idiomatic: when some mocked his frugality he said, "The Ma father and son spent themselves into ruin and cared nothing for the people—now their descendants beg for food. Is that an example to follow?"

sentences.zh: 世宗睿武孝文皇帝上

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, Sagely Martial and Filial in Civil Affairs — Part One
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong — Part One

sentences.zh: 太祖聖神恭肅文武孝皇帝下顯德二年（

translations.literal: Below: the Sagely, Divine, Reverent, Solemn, Civil, and Martial Filial Emperor Taizu, second year of Xiande (
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Shizong — Xiande, year 2 (

sentences.zh: 乙卯，公元九五五年）

translations.literal: Yimao, corresponding to the year 955 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: CE, cyclical year Yimao)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚辰，上以漕運自晉、漢以來不給斗耗，綱吏多以虧欠抵死，詔自今每斛給耗一鬥。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on day Gengchen, the Emperor, because since Jin and Han times canal transport had not granted surplus per dou and transport officers often paid with their lives for shortfalls, decreed that from now on one dou of surplus be granted per hu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on day Gengchen, the emperor decreed that because canal transport since Jin and Han times had granted no allowance for spillage, transport officers were often executed for shortages; henceforth one dou of surplus allowance would be granted per hu.

sentences.zh: 定難節度使李彝興以折德扆亦為節度使，與己並列，恥之，塞路不通周使。

translations.literal: Li Yixing, military governor of Dingnan, because Zhe Deyi was also made military governor and stood equal with him, felt shamed and blocked the roads so Zhou envoys could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Dingnan military governor Li Yixing, shamed that Zhe Deyi had also been made military governor as his equal, blocked the roads to Zhou envoys.

sentences.zh: 癸未，上謀於宰相，對曰：「夏州邊鎮，朝廷向來每加優借，府州褊小，得失不系重輕，旦宜撫諭彝興，庶全大體。」

translations.literal: On day Guiwei, the Emperor consulted the chancellors, who replied: "Xiazhou is a frontier command; the court has always shown it special favor. Fuzhou is narrow and small—its gain or loss does not bear on weighty matters. For now it is best to soothe and instruct Yixing, that the larger situation may be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: On day Guiwei the emperor consulted his chancellors, who said, "Xiazhou is a favored frontier post; Fuzhou is small and its fate is not critical. For now soothe Yixing and preserve the larger peace."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「德扆數年以來，盡忠戮力以拒劉氏，奈何一旦棄之！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "For several years Deyi has devoted loyalty and exhausted strength to resist the Liu house—how can we abandon him in a single day!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Deyi has for years served with loyal devotion against the Liu house—how can we cast him aside in a day!

sentences.zh: 且夏州惟產羊馬，貿易百貨，悉仰中國，我若絕之，彼何能為！」

translations.literal: Moreover, Xiazhou produces only sheep and horses; for trade in all goods it relies entirely on the Central Realm—if we cut it off, what can they do!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Xiazhou produces only sheep and horses and depends on us for all other trade—cut them off, and what can they do?"

sentences.zh: 乃遣供奉官齊藏珍繼招書責之，彝興惶恐謝罪。

translations.literal: He then sent the palace attendant Qi Cangzhen with a follow-up summons-letter rebuking him; Yixing, in fear, apologized for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: He sent palace attendant Qi Cangzhen with a stern summons; Yixing apologized in alarm.

sentences.zh: 戊子，蜀置威武軍於鳳州。

translations.literal: On day Wuzi, Shu established the Weiwu Army at Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On day Wuzi, Shu established the Weiwu Army at Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，初令翰林學士、兩省官舉令、錄。

translations.literal: On day Xinmao, for the first time Hanlin academicians and officials of the Two Departments were ordered to recommend magistrates and recorders.
translations.idiomatic: On day Xinmao, Hanlin academicians and officials of the Two Departments were for the first time required to nominate county magistrates and recorders.

sentences.zh: 除官之日，仍署舉者姓名，若貪穢敗官，並當連坐。

translations.literal: On the day of appointment, the recommender's name was still to be entered; if the appointee was greedy, corrupt, and ruined office, all were to share punishment.
translations.idiomatic: On appointment the recommender's name was to be recorded; if the nominee proved corrupt, the recommender would share the penalty.

sentences.zh: 契丹自晉、漢以來屢寇河北，輕騎深入，無籓籬之限，效野之民每困殺掠。

translations.literal: Since Jin and Han times the Khitan had repeatedly raided Hebei; light cavalry penetrated deep with no frontier barrier to limit them, and the people of the borderlands were constantly harried by killing and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin and Han times the Khitan had repeatedly raided Hebei; their light cavalry rode deep without frontier barriers, and border villagers suffered constant slaughter and plunder.

sentences.zh: 言事者稱深、冀之間有胡盧河，橫亙數百里，可浚之以限其奔突。

translations.literal: Memorialists said that between Shen and Ji there was the Hulu River, stretching across several hundred li, which could be dredged to limit their sudden charges.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists reported a Hulu River between Shen and Ji, hundreds of li long, that could be dredged to block Khitan raids.

sentences.zh: 是月，詔忠武節度使王彥超、彰信節度使韓通將兵夫浚胡盧河，築城於李晏口，留兵戍之。

translations.literal: That month, it was decreed that Wang Yanchao, military governor of Zhongwu, and Han Tong, military governor of Zhangxin, would lead laborers to dredge the Hulu River, build a city at Li Yankou, and leave troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wang Yanchao of Zhongwu and Han Tong of Zhangxin were ordered to dredge the Hulu River with labor troops, build a fortress at Li Yankou, and garrison it.

sentences.zh: 帝召德州刺史張藏英，問以備邊之策，藏英具陳地形要害，請列置戍兵，募邊人驍勇者，厚其稟給，自請將之，隨便宜討擊。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Zhang Zangying, prefect of Dezhou, and asked him for border-defense strategy; Zangying fully set forth the terrain's critical points, requested posting garrison troops in array, recruiting brave men among border people with generous rations, and asked to lead them himself to strike as opportunity allowed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Dezhou prefect Zhang Zangying and asked his views on border defense. Zangying mapped the critical terrain, proposed garrison posts, recruitment of brave border men on generous pay, and offered to lead them in opportunistic strikes.

sentences.zh: 帝皆從之，以藏英為沿邊巡檢招收都指揮使。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed all his proposals and made Zangying overall frontier inspection, recruitment, and command commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of this and appointed Zangying overall frontier inspection and recruitment commander.

sentences.zh: 藏英到官數月，募得千餘人。

translations.literal: Within several months of taking office Zangying recruited more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Within months of taking office Zangying had recruited over a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 王彥超等行視役者，嘗為契丹所圍。

translations.literal: When Wang Yanchao and others went to inspect the laborers, they were once surrounded by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Yanchao and others were inspecting the work crews, Khitan forces once surrounded them.

sentences.zh: 藏英引所募兵馳擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Zangying led his recruited troops in a swift attack and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zangying led his recruits in a swift charge and routed them.

sentences.zh: 自是契丹不敢涉胡盧河，河南之民始得休息。

translations.literal: From this time the Khitan did not dare cross the Hulu River, and the people south of the Yellow River first obtained rest.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Khitan dared not cross the Hulu River, and the people south of the Yellow River could at last breathe easier.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day of the cycle (day Gengzi), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the new moon of day Gengzi, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 蜀夔恭孝王仁毅卒。

translations.literal: Ren Yi, the Respectful and Filial Prince of Kui in Shu, died.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's Respectful and Filial Prince of Kui, Ren Yi, died.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，詔群臣極言得失，其略曰：「朕於卿大夫，才不能盡知，面不能盡識，若不採其言而觀其行，審其意而察其忠，則何以見器略之淺深，知任用之當否！

translations.literal: On day Renxu, the court was ordered that the ministers speak freely on gains and losses; the gist said: "We toward you ministers and great officers cannot fully know your talents or fully recognize your faces—if we do not take your words and observe your conduct, examine your intent and inspect your loyalty, how can we see the depth or shallowness of capacity and judgment, and know whether appointments are fitting!
translations.idiomatic: On day Renxu the court ordered ministers to speak freely of what was right and wrong in governance. The edict read in part: "I cannot know all your talents nor recognize all your faces. Unless I heed your words, watch your conduct, weigh your intent, and test your loyalty, how can I judge your capacity or know whether my appointments are sound?

sentences.zh: 若言之不入，罪實在予；

translations.literal: If words do not enter, the fault is truly in Us;
translations.idiomatic: If your words do not reach me, the fault is mine;

sentences.zh: 苟求之不言，咎將誰執！」

translations.literal: if We seek speech yet none is spoken, upon whom will blame fall!"
translations.idiomatic: but if I ask and you stay silent, upon whom will blame fall?"

sentences.zh: 唐主以中書侍郎、知尚書省嚴續為門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler made Yan Xu, vice director of the Secretariat and overseer of the Department of State Affairs, vice director of the Chancellery and co-equal councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler appointed Yan Xu, vice director of the Secretariat and overseer of the Department of State Affairs, as vice director of the Chancellery and co-equal councilor.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛未，以李晏口為靜安軍。

translations.literal: In the third month, on day Xinwei, Li Yankou was made the Jing'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on day Xinwei, Li Yankou was established as the Jing'an Army.

sentences.zh: 帝常憤廣明以來中國日蹙，及高平既捷，慨然有削平天下之志。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long resented that since the Guangming era the Central Realm daily shrank; once Gaoping was won, he was stirred with the ambition to level the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long resented how the Central Realm had shrunk since the Guangming era; after the victory at Gaoping he burned with ambition to reunify the empire.

sentences.zh: 會秦州民夷有詣大梁獻策請恢復舊疆者，帝納其言。

translations.literal: It happened that Han and tribal people of Qinzhou came to Daliang offering plans to recover the old frontiers; the Emperor adopted their words.
translations.idiomatic: When Han and tribal leaders from Qinzhou came to Daliang urging recovery of the old borders, the emperor took their advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 蜀主聞之，遣客省使趙季札案視邊備。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler heard of this and sent the guest-bureau commissioner Zhao Jizha to inspect border defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, the Shu ruler sent guest-bureau commissioner Zhao Jizha to inspect the border defenses.

sentences.zh: 季札素以文武才略自任，使還，奏稱：「雄武節度使韓繼勳、鳳州刺史王萬迪非將帥才，不足以御大敵。」

translations.literal: Jizha had always credited himself with civil and military talent and strategy; on returning from his mission he memorialized: "Han Jixun, military governor of Xiongwu, and Wang Wandi, prefect of Fengzhou, are not commander material and are insufficient to face a great enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Jizha had always prided himself on civil and military talent. On his return he reported that Xiongwu military governor Han Jixun and Fengzhou prefect Wang Wandi were not fit to command and could not face a major enemy."

sentences.zh: 蜀主問：「誰可往者？」

translations.literal: The Shu ruler asked: "Who can go?"
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler asked, "Who can go?"

sentences.zh: 季札自請行。

translations.literal: Jizha requested to go himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jizha volunteered himself.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以季札為雄武監軍使，仍以宿衛精兵千人為之部曲。

translations.literal: On day Bingshen, Jizha was made military inspector of Xiongwu, with a thousand elite palace-guard troops as his personal command.
translations.idiomatic: On day Bingshen, Jizha was made military inspector of Xiongwu with a thousand elite palace guards as his personal retinue.

sentences.zh: 帝以大梁城中迫隘，夏，四月，乙卯，詔展外城，先立標幟，俟今冬農隙興板築，東作動則罷之，更俟次年，以漸成之。

translations.literal: Because the city of Daliang was cramped and narrow, in summer, the fourth month, on day Yimao, it was decreed to extend the outer wall; markers were first set up, to await this winter's agricultural slack for rammed-earth work—when spring labor began it would halt, to await the following year, completing it gradually.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Daliang cramped, the emperor in the fourth month of summer, on day Yimao, ordered the outer walls extended. Markers were set out; construction would wait for the winter agricultural slack, halt when spring planting began, and resume the following year until the work was done.

sentences.zh: 且令自今葬埋皆出所標七里之外，其標內俟縣官分畫街衢、倉場、營廨之外，聽民隨便築室。

translations.literal: Moreover it was ordered that from now on all burials must be outside the markers by seven li; within the markers, after officials divided streets, granary yards, and barracks, the people were permitted to build dwellings as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Burials were henceforth to lie outside the markers by seven li; within them, once officials had laid out streets, granaries, and barracks, commoners might build houses as they wished.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，蜀主命知樞密院王昭遠按行北邊城寨及甲兵。

translations.literal: On day Bingchen, the Shu ruler ordered Wang Zhaoyuan, overseer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, to tour the northern border fortresses and armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: On day Bingchen the Shu ruler ordered bureau overseer Wang Zhaoyuan to inspect the northern border fortresses and armaments.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰相曰：「朕每思致治之方，未得其要，寢令不忘。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the chancellors: "We constantly think on the methods of bringing order, yet have not grasped the essentials—even in sleep We do not forget.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chancellors, "I constantly search for the way to good government but have not found its core; I cannot put it from my mind even in sleep.

sentences.zh: 又自唐、晉以來，吳、蜀、幽、并皆阻聲教，未能混壹，宜命近臣著《為君難為臣不易論》及《開邊策》各一篇，朕將覽焉。」

translations.literal: Moreover, since Tang and Jin, Wu, Shu, You, and Bing have all blocked Our transforming influence and have not been unified—near ministers should be ordered to compose one treatise each on 'The Difficulty of Being Ruler and the Difficulty of Being Minister' and on 'Border-Opening Strategy'; We shall review them."
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang and Jin, Wu, Shu, You, and Bing have all stood outside our civilizing reach. Order my close advisers each to write one essay on the difficulty of rule and service, and one on opening the frontiers—I will read them."

sentences.zh: 比部郎中王樸獻策，以為：「中國之失吳、蜀、幽、并，皆由失道。

translations.literal: Wang Pu of the Ministry of Revenue submitted a strategy, stating: "The Central Realm's loss of Wu, Shu, You, and Bing was all due to losing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue ministry director Wang Pu submitted a strategy arguing that the loss of Wu, Shu, You, and Bing had all come from abandoning the Way of rule.

sentences.zh: 今必先觀所以失之之原，然後知所以取之之術。

translations.literal: Now one must first observe the origin of how they were lost, and then one will know the method of how to take them.
translations.idiomatic: We must first study why they were lost, and only then will we know how to recover them.

sentences.zh: 其始失之也，莫不以君暗臣邪，兵驕民困，奸黨內熾，武夫外橫，因小致大，積微成著。

translations.literal: At the beginning of loss, none failed to begin with a dim ruler and wicked ministers, arrogant soldiers and distressed people, treacherous factions blazing within and martial men rampant without—small causes leading to great effects, minute accumulations becoming manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Every loss began the same way: dim rulers and corrupt ministers, arrogant armies and exhausted people, treachery within and warlords without—small faults swelling into ruin.

sentences.zh: 今欲取之，莫若反其所為而已。

translations.literal: Now wishing to take them back, nothing surpasses simply reversing what was done.
translations.idiomatic: To recover them, we need only reverse those errors.

sentences.zh: 夫進賢退不肖，所以收其才也；

translations.literal: Advancing the worthy and retiring the unworthy—this is how to gather their talent;
translations.idiomatic: Promote the worthy and dismiss the unworthy—that gathers talent;

sentences.zh: 恩隱誠信，所以結其心也；

translations.literal: favor, kindness, and sincere trust—this is how to bind their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: show kindness and keep faith—that binds men's hearts;

sentences.zh: 賞功罰罪，所以盡其力也；

translations.literal: rewarding merit and punishing crime—this is how to exhaust their strength;
translations.idiomatic: reward merit and punish crime—that brings forth their full effort;

sentences.zh: 去奢節用，所以豐其財也；

translations.literal: removing extravagance and economizing expenditure—this is how to enrich their finances;
translations.idiomatic: ban luxury and husband resources—that fills the treasury;

sentences.zh: 時使薄斂，所以阜其民也。

translations.literal: seasonably sending light levies—this is how to enrich the people.
translations.idiomatic: levy lightly and on time—that enriches the people.

sentences.zh: 俟群才既集，政事既治，財用既充，士民既附，然後舉而用之，功無不成矣！

translations.literal: Wait until all talent is gathered, government affairs are well ordered, finances are full, scholars and people are attached—then raise the army and use it, and no achievement will fail!
translations.idiomatic: When talent is assembled, government sound, coffers full, and the people loyal—then strike, and nothing will fail!

sentences.zh: 彼之人觀我有必取之勢，則知其情狀者願為間諜，知其山川者願為鄉導，民心既歸，天意必從矣。

translations.literal: When those people see that We have the momentum of certain conquest, those who know their situations will wish to be spies, those who know their mountains and rivers will wish to be guides—once popular hearts turn, Heaven's intent will surely follow.
translations.idiomatic: Once they see we mean to conquer, men who know their secrets will offer themselves as spies and guides; when the people's hearts turn, Heaven's mandate will follow.

sentences.zh: 凡攻取之道，必先其易者。

translations.literal: In all methods of attack and seizure, one must first take the easy.
translations.idiomatic: In conquest, always strike first where the foe is weakest.

sentences.zh: 唐與吾接境幾二千里，其勢易擾也。

translations.literal: Tang borders Us for nearly two thousand li; its position is easy to harass.
translations.idiomatic: Tang shares a border of nearly two thousand li with us—easy ground for harassment.

sentences.zh: 擾之當以無備之處為始，備東則擾西，備西則擾東，彼必奔走而救之。

translations.literal: To harass them one should begin where they are unprepared: if they guard the east, harass the west; if they guard the west, harass the east—they will surely rush about to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Harass them where they are unprepared: if they guard the east, strike the west; if the west, strike the east—they will rush back and forth to respond.

sentences.zh: 奔走之間，可以知其虛實強弱，然後避實擊虛，避強擊弱。

translations.literal: In their rushing about one can learn their emptiness and fullness, strength and weakness—then avoid the solid and strike the empty, avoid the strong and strike the weak.
translations.idiomatic: In that scrambling we will learn their strengths and gaps; then avoid the solid, strike the empty, shun the strong, hit the weak.

sentences.zh: 未須大舉，且以輕兵擾之。

translations.literal: There is no need for a great campaign yet—for now use light troops to harass them.
translations.idiomatic: No major campaign is needed yet—light troops alone will suffice to harry them.

sentences.zh: 南人懦怯，聞小有警，必悉師以救之。

translations.literal: Southerners are timid and cowardly; hearing even a small alarm, they will surely send all their armies to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The southerners are timid; at the slightest alarm they will mobilize every available unit.

sentences.zh: 師數動則民疲而財竭，不悉師則我可以乘虛取之。

translations.literal: If armies move repeatedly the people grow weary and finances are exhausted; if they do not send all armies, We can seize by exploiting emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated mobilizations will exhaust their people and treasury; if they fail to mobilize fully, we can seize ground at our leisure.

sentences.zh: 如此，江北諸州將悉為我有。

translations.literal: In this way the prefectures north of the Yangtze will all become Ours.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the prefectures north of the Yangtze will fall to us one by one.

sentences.zh: 既得江北，則用彼之民，行我之法，江南亦易取也。

translations.literal: Once the north bank is obtained, use their people and execute Our methods—the south bank will also be easy to take.
translations.idiomatic: Once we hold the north bank, we can govern with their people under our laws, and the south bank will be easy to take.

sentences.zh: 得江南則嶺南、巴蜀可傳檄而定。

translations.literal: Once the south bank is obtained, Lingnan and Ba-Shu can be settled by proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: With the south bank in hand, Lingnan and Ba-Shu can be won by proclamation alone.

sentences.zh: 南方既定，則燕地必望風內附。

translations.literal: Once the south is settled, the Yan region will surely turn to Us at the sight of Our banners.
translations.idiomatic: Once the south is settled, the Yan region will surely submit at our approach.

sentences.zh: 若其不至，移兵攻之，席捲可平矣。

translations.literal: If they do not come, shift troops to attack them—a rolling sweep can level them.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not, we move troops against them and sweep the land flat.

sentences.zh: 惟河東必死之寇，不可以恩信誘，當以強兵制之。

translations.literal: Only Hedong is an enemy that will fight to the death—it cannot be lured by favor and trust; strong troops must restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hedong is a foe that will fight to the death; favor and trust will not move them—only strong armies can hold them in check.

sentences.zh: 然彼自高平之敗，力竭氣沮，必未能為邊患。

translations.literal: Yet since their defeat at Gaoping their strength is exhausted and their spirit dejected—they surely cannot become a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since their defeat at Gaoping they are spent in strength and broken in spirit—they cannot threaten our borders for now.

sentences.zh: 宜且以為後圖，俟天下既平，然後伺間一舉可擒也。

translations.literal: For now they should be left for later planning; wait until the realm is already pacified, then watch for an opening and seize them in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Leave them for later; once the realm is pacified, watch for an opening and take them in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 今士卒精練，甲兵有備，群下畏法，諸將效力，期年之後可以出師，宜自夏秋蓄積實邊矣。」

translations.literal: Now soldiers are elite and trained, armor and weapons are prepared, subordinates fear law, generals exert effort—within a year's time troops can march; from this summer and autumn one should store provisions to fill the border."
translations.idiomatic: Our troops are now elite, our arms ready, our officers law-abiding and our generals eager. Within a year we may march; from this summer and autumn we should stock the border with provisions."

sentences.zh: 上欣然納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor gladly adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gladly accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 時群臣多守常偷安，所對少有可取者，惟樸神峻氣勁，有謀能斷，凡所規畫，皆稱上意，上由是重其器識。

translations.literal: At this time most ministers clung to routine and stole ease; their responses were rarely worth taking—only Pu was spirit-soaring and breath-forceful, possessed of strategy and able to decide; whatever he planned all matched the Emperor's intent, and the Emperor thereby valued his capacity and insight.
translations.idiomatic: Most ministers clung to routine and comfort, offering little of value; only Pu was forceful and decisive, and everything he proposed pleased the emperor, who came to value his judgment highly.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷左諫議大夫，知開封府事。

translations.literal: "Before long he was transferred to Left Remonstrance Grandee and overseer of Kaifeng prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: "Soon he was promoted to Left Remonstrance Grandee and put in charge of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 上謀取秦、鳳，求可將者。

translations.literal: The Emperor planned to take Qin and Feng and sought a commander able to lead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to seize Qin and Feng and sought a suitable commander.

sentences.zh: 王溥薦宣徽南院使、鎮安節度使向訓。

translations.literal: Wang Pu recommended Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and military governor of Zhen'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu recommended Xiang Xun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and military governor of Zhen'an.

sentences.zh: 上命訓與鳳翔節度使王景、客省使高唐昝居潤偕行。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Xun to go together with Wang Jing, military governor of Fengxiang, and Zan Jurun of Gaotang, guest-bureau commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Xun to proceed with Fengxiang military governor Wang Jing and Gaotang guest-bureau commissioner Zan Jurun.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊辰朔，景出兵自散關趣秦州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day of the cycle (day Wuchen), Jing led troops out from San Pass toward Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the new moon of day Wuchen, Jing marched from San Pass toward Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 敕天下寺院，非敕額者悉廢之。

translations.literal: It was ordered that monasteries throughout the realm without imperial plaque were all to be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished every monastery in the realm that lacked an imperial charter.

sentences.zh: 禁私度僧尼，凡欲出家者必俟祖父母、父母、伯叔之命。

translations.literal: Private ordination of monks and nuns was forbidden; all who wished to leave home life had to await the command of grandparents, parents, and uncles.
translations.idiomatic: Private ordination was forbidden; anyone wishing to become a monk or nun required permission from grandparents, parents, and uncles.

sentences.zh: 惟兩京、大名府、京兆府、青州聽設戒壇。

translations.literal: Only the Two Capitals, Daming prefecture, Jingzhao prefecture, and Qingzhou were permitted to establish ordination platforms.
translations.idiomatic: Ordination platforms were permitted only in the Two Capitals, Daming, Jingzhao, and Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 禁僧俗捨身、斷手足、煉指、掛燈、帶鉗之類幻惑流俗者。

translations.literal: Monks and laypeople were forbidden from self-sacrifice of the body, cutting off hands and feet, burning fingers, hanging lamps, wearing shackles, and similar practices that deluded common custom.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and lay devotees were forbidden such practices as offering their bodies, mutilating limbs, burning fingers, hanging lamps from the flesh, and wearing shackles—all delusions that misled the people.

sentences.zh: 令兩京及諸州每歲造僧帳，有死亡、歸俗，皆隨時開落。

translations.literal: The Two Capitals and all prefectures were ordered each year to compile monk registers; deaths and returns to lay life were all to be entered and struck in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Capitals and all prefectures were ordered to compile annual monk registers, striking names promptly upon death or return to lay life.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下寺院存者二千六百九十四，廢者三萬三百三十六，見僧四萬二千四百四十四，尼一萬八千七百五十六。

translations.literal: That year, monasteries remaining in the realm numbered 2,694; abolished numbered 30,336; registered monks numbered 42,444; nuns 18,756.
translations.idiomatic: That year 2,694 monasteries remained nationwide while 30,336 were abolished; registered monks numbered 42,444 and nuns 18,756.

sentences.zh: 王景拔黃牛等八寨。

translations.literal: Wang Jing captured Huangniu and seven other stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing took Huangniu and seven other fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，蜀主以捧聖控鶴都指揮使、保寧節度使李廷珪為北路行營都統，左衛聖步軍都指揮使高彥儔為招討使，武寧節度使呂彥珂副之，客省使趙崇韜為都監。

translations.literal: On day Wuyin, the Shu ruler appointed Li Tinggui, commander of the Sacred Crane Guard and military governor of Baoning, as overall commander of the northern route field headquarters; Gao Yanchou, commander of the Left Sacred Guard infantry, as punitive commissioner; Wuning military governor Lü Yanke as his deputy; and Reception Bureau envoy Zhao Chongtao as chief inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On day Wuyin, the Shu ruler named Li Tinggui—commander of the Sacred Crane Guard and military governor of Baoning—overall commander of the northern route army, with Left Sacred Guard infantry commander Gao Yanchou as punitive commissioner, Wuning military governor Lü Yanke as his deputy, and Reception Bureau envoy Zhao Chongtao as chief inspector.

sentences.zh: 蜀趙季札至德陽，聞周師入境，懼不敢進，上書求解邊任還奏事，先遣輜重及妓妾西歸。

translations.literal: Shu officer Zhao Jizha reached Deyang, heard that Zhou forces had entered the realm, feared and dared not advance, memorialized requesting release from frontier duty to return and report on affairs, and first sent baggage trains, courtesans, and concubines westward homeward.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shu officer Zhao Jizha reached Deyang and learned that Zhou armies had crossed the border, he was too frightened to advance. He asked to be relieved of his frontier command so he could return to court, and sent his baggage train, entertainers, and concubines back west ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，單騎馳入成都，眾以為奔敗，莫不震恐。

translations.literal: On day Dinghai, he rode alone at full speed into Chengdu; the multitude thought he had fled in defeat, and none were not shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: On day Dinghai he galloped into Chengdu alone. Everyone assumed he had fled in defeat, and panic spread through the city.

sentences.zh: 蜀主問以機事，皆不能對。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler questioned him about military affairs; he could answer none of them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shu ruler questioned him about the military situation, he could answer nothing.

sentences.zh: 蜀主怒，系之御史台，甲午，斬之於崇禮門。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler was angry, imprisoned him at the Censorate, and on day Jiawu executed him at Chongli Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler, enraged, had him imprisoned by the Censorate and, on day Jiawu, executed him at Chongli Gate.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚子，上親錄囚於內苑。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on day Gengzi, the emperor personally reviewed prisoners in the inner park.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on day Gengzi, Emperor Shizong personally heard criminal cases in the inner palace grounds.

sentences.zh: 有汝州民馬遇，父及弟為吏所冤死，屢經覆按，不能自伸，上臨問，始得其實，人以為神。

translations.literal: There was a man of Ruzhou named Ma Yu, whose father and younger brother had been wrongly killed by officials; though repeatedly reinvestigated, he could not clear himself. When the emperor questioned him in person, the truth was finally obtained, and people regarded it as miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner of Ruzhou named Ma Yu had seen his father and brother wrongly killed by officials. Repeated reinvestigations had failed to clear the case until Emperor Shizong questioned him in person and finally got at the truth. People took it as proof of his almost supernatural judgment.

sentences.zh: 由是諸長吏無不親察獄訟。

translations.literal: From this, all senior officials none failed to personally examine lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: After that, senior officials everywhere began to examine lawsuits in person.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，西師與蜀李廷珪等戰於威武城東，不利，排陳使濮州刺史胡立等為蜀所擒。

translations.literal: On day Renyin, the western army fought Li Tinggui and others of Shu east of Weiwu city, unfavorably; array commissioner Hu Li, prefect of Puzhou, and others were captured by Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On day Renyin the western army fought Li Tinggui and other Shu commanders east of Weiwu city and was defeated. Array commissioner Hu Li, prefect of Puzhou, and others were captured.

sentences.zh: 丁未，蜀主遣間使如北漢及唐，欲與之俱出兵以制周，北漢主、唐主皆許之。

translations.literal: On day Dingwei, the Shu ruler sent secret envoys to Northern Han and Southern Tang, wishing jointly to dispatch troops to check Zhou; the Northern Han ruler and the Southern Tang ruler both agreed.
translations.idiomatic: On day Dingwei the Shu ruler sent secret envoys to Northern Han and Southern Tang, hoping to coordinate a joint campaign against Zhou. Both rulers agreed.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以彰信節度使韓通充西南行營馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: On day Jiyou, Zhangxin military governor Han Tong was appointed chief adjutant of cavalry and infantry for the southwestern field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On day Jiyou, Zhangxin military governor Han Tong was made chief adjutant of cavalry and infantry for the southwestern field army.

sentences.zh: 戊午，南漢主殺禎州節度使通王弘政，於是高祖之諸子盡矣。

translations.literal: On day Wuwu, the Southern Han ruler killed Wang Hongzheng, Prince of Tong and military governor of Zhenzhou; with this, all of Gaozu's sons were gone.
translations.idiomatic: On day Wuwu the Southern Han ruler executed Wang Hongzheng, Prince of Tong and military governor of Zhenzhou. With that, all of Gaozu's sons were gone.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以樞密院承旨清河張美為右領軍大將軍、權點檢三司事。

translations.literal: On day Renxu, Zhang Mei of Qinghe, Hanlin commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was appointed Right Leading Army Grand General and acting inspector of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: On day Renxu, Zhang Mei of Qinghe, a Hanlin commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Right Leading Army Grand General and acting inspector of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在澶州，美掌州之金谷隸三司者，帝或私有所求，美曲為供副。

translations.literal: Initially, when Emperor Shizong was at Cazhou, Mei managed the prefecture's treasury funds subordinate to the Three Offices; Emperor Shizong sometimes had private requests, and Mei bent rules to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Shizong was stationed at Cazhou, Zhang Mei oversaw the prefecture's treasury funds under the Three Offices. When Shizong occasionally made private requests, Mei contrived to satisfy them.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之怒，恐傷帝意，但徙美為濮州馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: Taizu heard of it and was angry; fearing to hurt Emperor Shizong's feelings, he only transferred Mei to be cavalry and infantry adjutant at Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu heard of it and was furious, but fearing to wound Emperor Shizong's feelings he merely transferred Mei to be cavalry and infantry adjutant at Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 美治財精敏，當時鮮及，故帝以利權授之。

translations.literal: Mei was acute in managing finances, rarely matched in his time; therefore Emperor Shizong entrusted him with fiscal authority.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mei was exceptionally sharp at managing finances, and few in his day could match him, so Emperor Shizong gave him control over revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝征伐四方，用度不乏，美之力也，然思其在澶州所為，終不以公忠待之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong campaigned in the four directions, and expenditures never lacked—the credit was Mei's; yet remembering what he had done at Cazhou, he never treated him with the trust due a loyal public servant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong's campaigns in every direction never ran short of funds, and much of that was Mei's doing. Yet remembering his conduct at Cazhou, Shizong never treated him with the trust owed a loyal public servant.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁卯朔，以王景兼西南行營都招討使，向訓兼行營兵馬都監。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the new moon of day Dingmao, Wang Jing was additionally made overall punitive commissioner of the southwestern field headquarters, and Xiang Xun was made field army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the new moon of day Dingmao, Wang Jing was also made overall punitive commissioner of the southwestern field army, and Xiang Xun was made its army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 宰相以景等久無功。

translations.literal: The chancellors, on the grounds that Jing and the others had long been without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors argued that Jing and his colleagues had achieved nothing after a long campaign.

sentences.zh: 饋運不繼，固請罷兵。

translations.literal: Supplies could not keep up; they firmly requested to halt the army.
translations.idiomatic: With supplies failing to keep up, they strongly urged that the campaign be halted.

sentences.zh: 帝命太祖皇帝往視之，還，言秦、鳳可取之狀，帝從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong ordered Zhao Kuangyin—the palace guard commander, known retrospectively as Emperor Taizu—to go inspect; when he returned, he reported the situation that Qin and Feng could be taken, and Emperor Shizong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong ordered Zhao Kuangyin, the palace guard commander whom Sima Guang retrospectively styles Emperor Taizu, to inspect the front. On his return he reported that Qin and Feng could be taken, and Shizong accepted his judgment.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁未，中書侍郎、同平章事景范罷判三司，尋以父喪罷政事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day Dingwei, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Ranking Censor-in-Chief Jing Fan was removed from overseeing the Three Offices; soon afterward, on account of his father's death, he was dismissed from government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on day Dingwei, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Ranking Censor-in-Chief Jing Fan was removed from overseeing the Three Offices, and soon afterward left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 王景等敗蜀兵，獲將卒三百。

translations.literal: Wang Jing and others defeated Shu troops and captured three hundred officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing and his colleagues defeated Shu forces and captured three hundred officers and men.

sentences.zh: 己未，蜀主遣通奏使、知樞密院、武泰節度使伊審征如行營慰扶，仍督戰。

translations.literal: On day Jiwei, the Shu ruler sent memorial envoy Yin Shenzheng, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military governor of Wutai, to the field headquarters to comfort the troops and supervise battle.
translations.idiomatic: On day Jiwei the Shu ruler sent memorial envoy Yin Shenzheng—commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military governor of Wutai—to the front to console the troops and press the fighting.

sentences.zh: 帝以縣官久不鑄錢，而民間多銷錢為器皿及佛像，錢益少，九月，丙寅朔，敕始立監採銅鑄錢，自非縣官法物、軍器及寺觀鐘磐鈸鐸之類聽留外，自餘民間銅器、佛像，五十日內悉令輸官，給其直；

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, because the government had long not cast coins while the common people extensively melted coins into vessels and Buddha images so that coin grew ever scarcer—in the ninth month, on the new moon of day Bingyin, decreed establishing bureaus to mine copper and cast coins.
