Except for official ritual vessels, military equipment, and temple bells, chimes, cymbals, and clappers, which were permitted to be retained, as for all other common copperware and Buddha images, within fifty days all were ordered surrendered to the government, and payment would be given;
translations.idiomatic: Because the government had long ceased minting coin while commoners melted cash into utensils and Buddha images until currency grew scarce, Emperor Shizong—in the ninth month, on the new moon of day Bingyin—decreed the establishment of mints to mine copper and cast coin. Apart from official ritual objects, weapons, and temple bells, chimes, cymbals, and clappers, all other copperware and Buddha images in private hands were to be surrendered to the state within fifty days in exchange for payment;

sentences.zh: 過期隱匿不輸，五斤以上其罪死，不及者論刑有差。

translations.literal: Those who after the deadline concealed and did not surrender—five jin or more, the crime was death; for less, penalties were differentiated by degree.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who hid goods past the deadline faced death if the amount was five jin or more; lesser amounts brought graded punishments.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「卿輩勿以毀佛為疑。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attending ministers: "You all must not doubt this on the grounds of destroying Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong told his attending ministers, "Do not doubt this policy because it destroys Buddha images.

sentences.zh: 夫佛以善道化人，苟志於善，斯奉佛矣。

translations.literal: For Buddha uses the good Way to transform people; if one is devoted to goodness, that is worshipping Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha teaches people through the path of goodness. Whoever is devoted to goodness is already honoring Buddha.

sentences.zh: 彼銅像豈所謂佛邪！

translations.literal: Are those copper images what is called Buddha!
translations.idiomatic: Are those copper statues what Buddha really is?

sentences.zh: 且吾聞佛志在利人，雖頭目猶捨以佈施，若朕身可以濟民，亦非所惜也。」

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard Buddha's aim lies in benefiting people—even head and eyes he would still give up to bestow; if my person can relieve the people, that too is nothing to begrudge."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I have heard that Buddha's purpose is to benefit others, giving even his head and eyes in charity. If my own person can save the people, I will not begrudge that either."

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：若周世宗，可謂仁矣！

translations.literal: Your subject Guang remarks: Consider Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou—one may call him benevolent!
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Guang remarks: Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou may truly be called benevolent!

sentences.zh: 不愛其身而愛民；

translations.literal: He did not love his own person but loved the people;
translations.idiomatic: He did not spare himself, but cared for his people;

sentences.zh: 若周世宗，可謂明矣！

translations.literal: Consider Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou—one may call him enlightened!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou may truly be called enlightened!

sentences.zh: 不以無益廢有益。

translations.literal: He did not discard what was beneficial for what was not beneficial.
translations.idiomatic: He did not sacrifice what was useful for what was useless.

sentences.zh: 蜀李廷珪遣先鋒都指揮使李進據馬嶺寨，又遣奇兵出斜谷，屯白澗，又分兵出鳳州之北唐倉鎮及黃花谷，絕周糧道。

translations.literal: Shu Li Tinggui sent vanguard commander Li Jin to hold Maling stockade, also sent irregular troops out through Xie Valley to encamp at Baixian, also divided forces out through Tangcang post north of Fengzhou and Huanghuagu Valley to cut Zhou supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's Li Tinggui sent vanguard commander Li Jin to hold Maling camp, dispatched a flanking force through Xie Valley to encamp at Baixian, and split troops through Tangcang north of Fengzhou and through Huanghuagu Valley to sever Zhou supply lines.

sentences.zh: 閏月，王景遣裨將張建雄將兵二千抵黃花，又遣兵千人趣唐倉，扼蜀歸路。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Wang Jing sent subordinate general Zhang Jianxiong to lead two thousand troops to Huanghua, also sent a thousand troops toward Tangcang to block the Shu line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Wang Jing sent subordinate general Zhang Jianxiong with two thousand men to Huanghua and another thousand toward Tangcang to cut off the Shu army's retreat.

sentences.zh: 蜀染院使王巒將兵出唐倉，與建雄戰於黃花，蜀兵敗，奔唐倉，遇周兵，又敗，虜巒及其將士三千人。

translations.literal: Shu Dye House commissioner Wang Luan led troops out from Tangcang and fought Jianxiong at Huanghua; Shu troops were defeated, fled to Tangcang, met Zhou troops, were defeated again, and Luan with his officers and soldiers three thousand were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Dye House commissioner Wang Luan marched out of Tangcang and fought Jianxiong at Huanghua. The Shu force was beaten, fled toward Tangcang, ran into Zhou troops, and was defeated again. Luan and three thousand of his officers and men were captured.

sentences.zh: 馬嶺、白澗兵皆潰，李廷珪、高彥儔等退保青泥嶺。

translations.literal: Troops at Maling and Baixian all collapsed; Li Tinggui, Gao Yanchou, and others withdrew to hold Qingni Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The forces at Maling and Baixian broke and fled. Li Tinggui, Gao Yanchou, and the others fell back to Qingni Ridge.

sentences.zh: 蜀雄武節度使兼侍中韓繼勳棄秦州，奔還成都、觀察判宮趙玭舉城降，斜谷援兵亦潰。

translations.literal: Shu Xiongwu military governor and palace attendant Han Jixun abandoned Qinzhou and fled back to Chengdu; observation aide Zhao Pi surrendered the city; relief troops from Xie Valley also collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xiongwu military governor and palace attendant Han Jixun abandoned Qinzhou and fled to Chengdu, while observation aide Zhao Pi surrendered the city. The relief force from Xie Valley also disintegrated.

sentences.zh: 成、階二州皆降，蜀人振恐。

translations.literal: Cheng and Jie prefectures both surrendered; Shu people were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Jie prefectures both submitted, and panic spread through Shu.

sentences.zh: 玭，澶州人也。

translations.literal: Pi was a man of Cazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pi was a native of Cazhou.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以玭為節度使，范質固爭以為不可，乃以為郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong wished to make Pi a military governor; Fan Zhi strongly argued it was not permissible; he was therefore made prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong wanted to make Zhao Pi a military governor, but Fan Zhi strongly objected, and Pi was appointed prefect of Ezhou instead.

sentences.zh: 壬子，百官入賀，帝舉酒屬王溥曰：「邊功之成，卿擇帥之力也！」

translations.literal: On day Renzi, the hundred officials entered to offer congratulations; Emperor Shizong raised his cup and addressed Wang Pu, saying: "The achievement of the frontier campaign—the power lies in your choosing commanders!"
translations.idiomatic: On day Renzi the court officials came to offer congratulations. Emperor Shizong raised his cup toward Wang Pu and said, "This frontier victory is owed to your skill in choosing commanders!"

sentences.zh: 甲子，上與將相食於萬歲殿，因言：「兩日大寒，朕於宮中食珍膳，深愧無功於民而坐享於祿，既不能躬耕而食，惟當親冒矢石為民除害，差可自安耳！」

translations.literal: On day Jiazi, the emperor dined with generals and chancellors in the Hall of Longevity and, continuing, said: "For two days the cold has been severe; within the palace I eat fine fare, and deeply ashamed that I have no achievement for the people yet sit enjoying salary—since I cannot personally plow and eat, I should only personally expose myself to arrows and stones to remove harms for the people; only thus may I somewhat set my mind at ease!"
translations.idiomatic: On day Jiazi Emperor Shizong dined with his generals and chancellors in the Hall of Longevity and said, "These past two days have been bitterly cold. I eat rich food in the palace while doing nothing for the people, and I am deeply ashamed to enjoy my salary. Since I cannot plow for my own bread, I can at least face arrows and stones myself to remove threats from the people. Only that can somewhat ease my conscience!"

sentences.zh: 乙丑，蜀李廷珪上表待罪。

translations.literal: On day Yichou, Shu Li Tinggui submitted a memorial awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: On day Yichou Shu's Li Tinggui submitted a memorial accepting blame.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬申，伊審征至成都請罪。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on day Renshen, Yin Shenzheng reached Chengdu to plead guilty.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on day Renshen Yin Shenzheng reached Chengdu to plead guilty.

sentences.zh: 皆釋之。

translations.literal: Both were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Both were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 蜀主致書於帝請和，自稱大蜀皇帝，帝怒其抗禮，不答。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler sent a letter to Emperor Shizong seeking peace, styling himself Emperor of Great Shu; Emperor Shizong was angry at his breach of protocol and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler wrote to Emperor Shizong seeking peace, styling himself Emperor of Great Shu. Shizong, angered by this breach of protocol, did not answer.

sentences.zh: 蜀主愈恐，聚兵糧於劍門、白帝，為守禦之備，募兵既多，用度不足，始鑄鐵錢，榷境內鐵器，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler grew ever more fearful, gathered troops and grain at Jianmen and Baidi for defensive preparations; having recruited many soldiers, expenses were insufficient, and they began casting iron coins and monopolizing ironware within the borders—the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler grew more frightened still. He stockpiled troops and grain at Jianmen and Baidi to prepare a defense. Recruitment swelled until expenses could not keep up, and the court began minting iron coin and monopolizing iron goods within the realm. The people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 唐主性和柔，好文章，而喜人順己，由是諂諛之臣多進用，政事日亂。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler's nature was gentle and soft; he loved literature and favored those who complied with him; from this flatterers were widely advanced, and governance daily grew chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler was mild by nature and loved literature. He delighted in those who agreed with him, so flatterers rose in number and government grew more chaotic by the day.

sentences.zh: 既克建州，破湖南，益驕，有吞天下之志。

translations.literal: Having taken Jianzhou and broken Hunan, he grew ever prouder, with ambition to swallow all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: After conquering Jianzhou and crushing Hunan, he grew ever prouder and set his sights on ruling all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 李守貞、慕容彥超之叛，皆為之出師，遙為聲援。

translations.literal: The rebellions of Li Shouzhen and Murong Yanchao—both times he sent out armies for them, lending distant support.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shouzhen and Murong Yanchao rebelled, he sent armies on each occasion to lend them distant support.

sentences.zh: 又遣使自海道通契丹及北漢，約共圖中國。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys by sea route to connect with the Khitan and Northern Han, agreeing jointly to scheme against China.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys by sea to contact the Khitan and Northern Han, agreeing to join in a plot against the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 值中國多事，未暇與之校。

translations.literal: It happened that China had many affairs, and there was no leisure to contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: China was beset with troubles at the time and had no leisure to confront him.

sentences.zh: 先是，每冬淮水淺涸，唐人常發兵戍守，謂之「把淺」。

translations.literal: Earlier, every winter when the Huai River ran shallow and dry, Southern Tang people often dispatched troops to garrison—what they called "holding the shallows" (ba qian).
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, each winter when the Huai ran low, Southern Tang regularly posted troops to guard the shallows in what they called "holding the shallows" (ba qian).

sentences.zh: 壽州監軍吳廷紹以為疆場無事，坐費資糧，悉罷之。

translations.literal: Shouzhou army supervisor Wu Tingshao thought the border was without incident and sitting wasted supplies; he abolished them all.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhou army supervisor Wu Tingshao decided the frontier was quiet and that the posts wasted supplies, and abolished them all.

sentences.zh: 清淮節度使劉仁贍上表固爭，不能得。

translations.literal: Huaiqing military governor Liu Renzhan memorialized strongly protesting but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiqing military governor Liu Renzhan memorialized in strong protest but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙未朔，帝以李穀為淮南道前軍行營都部署兼知廬、壽等行府事，以忠武節度使王彥超副之，督侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤等十二將以伐唐。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of day Yimao, Emperor Shizong appointed Li Gu as overall commander of the Huainan Route advance army field headquarters and concurrently administering the field administration of Lu, Shou, and others, with Zhongwu military governor Wang Yanchao as deputy, supervising Han Lingkun, commander of the palace guard cavalry, and twelve other generals to attack Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of day Yimao, Emperor Shizong made Li Gu overall commander of the Huainan advance army and administrator of the field headquarters at Lu, Shou, and neighboring posts, with Zhongwu military governor Wang Yanchao as his deputy. He ordered palace guard cavalry commander Han Lingkun and eleven other generals to attack Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 令坤，磁州武安人也。

translations.literal: Lingkun was a man of Wu'an in Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun was a native of Wu'an in Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 汴水自唐末潰決，自埇橋東南悉為污澤。

translations.literal: The Bian River, since the end of Tang, had broken and burst; from Yongqiao southeast all became morass.
translations.idiomatic: Since late Tang the Bian River had burst its banks, and from Yongqiao southeastward the land had turned into marsh.

sentences.zh: 上謀擊唐，先命武寧節度使武行德發民夫，因故堤疏導之，東至泗上。

translations.literal: The emperor planned to attack Southern Tang and first ordered Wuning military governor Wu Xingde to mobilize corvee labor, following the old dikes to dredge and channel it, east to Si prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Planning an attack on Southern Tang, Emperor Shizong first ordered Wuning military governor Wu Xingde to mobilize laborers to dredge the old channel eastward as far as Si prefecture.

sentences.zh: 議者皆以為難成，上曰：「數年之後，必獲其利。」

translations.literal: Discussants all thought it hard to accomplish; the emperor said: "Within several years, the benefit will certainly be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Critics all said it could not be done. Emperor Shizong replied, "In a few years we will surely reap the benefit."

sentences.zh: 丁未，上與侍臣論刑賞，上曰：「朕必不因怒刑人，因喜賞人。」

translations.literal: On day Dingwei, the emperor with attending ministers discussed punishments and rewards; the emperor said: "I certainly will not punish people because of anger, nor reward people because of pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: On day Dingwei Emperor Shizong discussed punishments and rewards with his attending ministers. He said, "I will never punish anyone in anger or reward anyone in a fit of pleasure."

sentences.zh: 先是，大梁城中民侵街衢為捨，通大車者蓋寡，上悉命直而廣之，廣者至三十步。

translations.literal: Earlier, within Daliang city common people encroached on streets and avenues building dwellings, so those passing large carts were few; the emperor ordered all straightened and widened, some places to thirty paces.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Daliang commoners had built into the streets until few large carts could pass. Emperor Shizong ordered the roads straightened and widened, in places to thirty paces.

sentences.zh: 又遷墳墓於標外。

translations.literal: Grave mounds were also moved outside the markers.
translations.idiomatic: Graves were also moved outside the boundary markers.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「近廣京城，於存歿擾動誠多。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Recently, expanding the capital city, disturbance to the living and dead is indeed much.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong said, "In expanding the capital lately, we have disturbed the living and the dead alike.

sentences.zh: 怨謗之語，朕自當之，他日終為人利。」

translations.literal: Words of resentment and slander—I myself will bear them; one day it will ultimately benefit the people."
translations.idiomatic: Let the complaints fall on me. In time this will benefit the people."

sentences.zh: 王景等圍鳳州，韓通分兵城固鎮以絕蜀之援兵。

translations.literal: Wang Jing and others besieged Fengzhou; Han Tong divided troops to fortify Chenggu post to cut off Shu relief.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing and his colleagues besieged Fengzhou while Han Tong detached troops to hold Chenggu and block Shu reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 戊申，克鳳州，擒蜀威武節度使王環及都監趙崇溥等將士五千人。

translations.literal: On day Wushen, Fengzhou was taken; Shu Weiwu military governor Wang Huan and inspector Zhao Chongbo and others, five thousand officers and soldiers, were captured.
translations.idiomatic: On day Wushen Fengzhou fell. Shu's Weiwu military governor Wang Huan, inspector Zhao Chongbo, and five thousand officers and men were captured.

sentences.zh: 崇溥不食而死。

translations.literal: Chongbo died from refusing food.
translations.idiomatic: Chongbo starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 環，真定人也。

translations.literal: Huan was a man of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan was a native of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，制曲赦秦、鳳、階、成境內，所獲蜀將士，願留者優其俸賜，願去者給資裝而遣之。

translations.literal: On day Yimao, a partial amnesty was decreed for Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng; captured Shu officers and soldiers—those wishing to stay were given favorable salary and awards, those wishing to leave were given funds and equipment and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: On day Yimao a partial amnesty was issued for Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng. Captured Shu officers and soldiers who wished to remain were given generous pay and rewards; those who wished to leave were supplied with funds and equipment and sent home.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「用慰眾情，免違物性，其四州之民，二稅征科之外，凡蜀人所立諸色科徭，悉罷之。」

translations.literal: The decree said: "To appease the feelings of the multitude and avoid violating their nature—within the four prefectures, outside the two-tax levies, all miscellaneous corvees and levies established by Shu people are entirely abolished."
translations.idiomatic: The decree read, "To soothe the people and avoid violating their ways: in these four prefectures, beyond the regular two-tax assessments, every levy and corvee imposed under Shu rule is abolished."

sentences.zh: 唐人聞周兵將至而懼，劉仁贍神氣自若，部分守禦，無異平日，眾情稍安。

translations.literal: Southern Tang people, hearing Zhou troops were about to arrive, were fearful; Liu Renzhan's spirit was calm as usual, arranged defense no different from ordinary days, and popular sentiment was slightly calmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Southern Tang learned that Zhou armies were approaching, fear spread—but Liu Renzhan remained as composed as ever, arranging defenses as on any other day, and morale steadied somewhat.

sentences.zh: 唐主以神武統軍劉彥貞為北面行營都部署，將兵二萬趣壽州，奉化節度使、同平章事皇甫暉為應援使，常州團練使姚鳳為應援都監，將兵三萬屯定遠。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler appointed Liu Yanzhen, Shenwu army commander, as overall commander of the northern route field headquarters, leading twenty thousand troops toward Shouzhou; Fenghua military governor and Co-Ranking Censor-in-Chief Huangfu Hui as relief commander; Changzhou regimental trainer Yao Feng as relief chief inspector, leading thirty thousand troops encamped at Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler made Shenwu army commander Liu Yanzhen overall commander of the northern route army and sent him with twenty thousand men toward Shouzhou. Fenghua military governor and Co-Ranking Censor-in-Chief Huangfu Hui was made relief commander, and Changzhou regimental trainer Yao Feng relief chief inspector with thirty thousand men encamped at Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 召鎮南節度使宋齊丘還金陵，謀國難，以翰林承旨、戶部尚書殷崇義為吏部尚書、知樞密院。

translations.literal: He summoned Zhennan military governor Song Qiuqiu back to Jinling to consult on the national crisis, and made Hanlin commissioner and Minister of Revenue Yin Chongyi Minister of Personnel and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Zhennan military governor Song Qiqiu to Jinling to plan for the crisis and appointed Hanlin commissioner and Minister of Revenue Yin Chongyi Minister of Personnel and commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 李穀等為浮梁，自正陽濟淮。

translations.literal: Li Gu and others built a pontoon bridge, crossing the Huai from Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu and his colleagues built a pontoon bridge and crossed the Huai from Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲戌，穀奏王彥超敗唐兵二千餘人於壽州城下，己卯，又奏先鋒都指揮使白延遇敗唐兵千餘人於山口鎮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on day Jiaxu, Gu memorialized that Wang Yanchao defeated Southern Tang troops of more than two thousand beneath Shouzhou city; on day Jiji, he further memorialized that vanguard commander Bai Yanyu defeated Southern Tang troops of more than a thousand at Shankou post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on day Jiaxu Li Gu reported that Wang Yanchao had defeated more than two thousand Southern Tang troops below Shouzhou. On day Jiji he reported that vanguard commander Bai Yanyu had beaten more than a thousand Southern Tang soldiers at Shankou.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，樞密使兼侍中韓忠正公鄭仁誨卒。

translations.literal: On day Bingxu, Hanlin Messenger and Palace Attendant Duke of Loyally Upright Han Zheng Zheng Rensheng died.
translations.idiomatic: On day Bingxu Hanlin Messenger and Palace Attendant Duke of Loyally Upright Zheng Rensheng died.

sentences.zh: 上臨其喪，近臣奏稱歲道非便，上曰：「君臣義重，何日時之有！」

translations.literal: The emperor attended his funeral; close attendants memorialized that the season was inauspicious; the emperor said: "The righteousness between ruler and minister is weighty—what talk of seasons!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong went to the funeral. Close attendants said the season was inauspicious, but he replied, "The bond between ruler and minister outweighs such concerns—what talk of seasons!"

sentences.zh: 往哭盡哀。

translations.literal: He went and wept with full grief.
translations.idiomatic: He went and mourned with full grief.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘俶遣元帥府判官陳彥禧入貢，帝以詔諭弘俶，使出兵擊唐。

translations.literal: Wuyue King Hongchu sent Marshal's Headquarters aide Chen Yanxi to present tribute; Emperor Shizong with an edict instructed Hongchu to dispatch troops to attack Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyue King Hongchu sent Marshal's Headquarters aide Chen Yanxi to pay tribute. Emperor Shizong issued an edict urging Hongchu to send troops against Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 太祖聖神恭肅文武孝皇帝下顯德三年（

translations.literal: Below: the Sagely, Divine, Reverent, Solemn, Civil, and Martial Filial Emperor Taizu, Xiande year 3 (
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Shizong — Xiande, year 3 (

sentences.zh: 丙辰，公元九五六年）

translations.literal: Bingchen, corresponding to the year 956 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: Bingchen, corresponding to the year 956 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙午，以王環為右驍衛大將軍，賞其不降也。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on day Bingwu, Wang Huan was made Right Xiaoqiwei Grand General, rewarding him for not surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on day Bingwu Wang Huan was made Right Xiaoqiwei Grand General as a reward for refusing to surrender.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，李穀奏敗唐兵千餘人於上窯。

translations.literal: On day Dingyou, Li Gu memorialized defeating Southern Tang troops of more than a thousand at Shangyao.
translations.idiomatic: On day Dingyou Li Gu reported defeating more than a thousand Southern Tang troops at Shangyao.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，發開封府、曹、滑、鄭州之民十餘萬築大梁外城。

translations.literal: On day Wuxu, more than a hundred thousand people of Kaifeng prefecture, Cao, Hua, and Zheng prefectures were mobilized to build Daliang's outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: On day Wuxu more than a hundred thousand laborers from Kaifeng, Cao, Hua, and Zheng were mobilized to build Daliang's outer wall.

sentences.zh: 庚子，帝下詔親征淮南，以宣徽南院使、鎮安節度使向訓權東京留守，端明殿學士王樸副之，彰信節度使韓通權點檢侍衛司及在京內外都巡檢。

translations.literal: On day Gengzi, Emperor Shizong issued an edict for a personal campaign to Huainan, appointing Xuannwei South Court envoy and Zhen'an military governor Xiang Xun acting Eastern Capital regent, with Duanming Hall academician Wang Pu as deputy; Zhangxin military governor Han Tong acting inspector of the Palace Guard Bureau and overall metropolitan and capital patrols.
translations.idiomatic: On day Gengzi Emperor Shizong decreed a personal campaign to Huainan. He made Xuannwei South Court envoy and Zhen'an military governor Xiang Xun acting Eastern Capital regent, with Duanming Hall academician Wang Pu as his deputy, and Zhangxin military governor Han Tong acting inspector of the Palace Guard and overall patrol commander inside and outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 命侍衛都指揮使、歸德節度使李重進將兵先赴正陽，河陽節度使白重贊將親兵三千屯穎上。

translations.literal: He ordered Palace Guard commander and Guide military governor Li Chongjin to lead troops first to Zhengyang; Heyang military governor Bai Chongzan to lead three thousand personal troops encamped at Yingshang.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered palace guard commander and Guide military governor Li Chongjin to march first to Zhengyang, and Heyang military governor Bai Chongzan to encamp three thousand personal troops at Yingshang.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，帝發大梁。

translations.literal: On day Renyin, Emperor Shizong departed Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On day Renyin Emperor Shizong set out from Daliang.

sentences.zh: 李穀攻壽州，久不克。

translations.literal: Li Gu attacked Shouzhou but for long could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu besieged Shouzhou but could not capture it for a long time.

sentences.zh: 唐劉彥貞引兵救之，至來遠鎮，距壽州二百里，又以戰艦數百艘趣正陽，為攻浮梁之勢。

translations.literal: Southern Tang Liu Yanzhen led troops to relieve it, reaching Laiyuan post, two hundred li from Shouzhou; also with several hundred warships pressed toward Zhengyang, taking the posture of attacking the pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang's Liu Yanzhen marched to relieve the city, reaching Laiyuan—two hundred li from Shouzhou—and sent several hundred warships toward Zhengyang as if to strike the pontoon bridge.

sentences.zh: 李穀畏之，召將佐謀曰：「我軍不能水戰，若賊斷浮梁，則腹背受敵，皆不歸矣！

translations.literal: Li Gu feared this, summoned officers and aides to consult, saying: "Our army cannot fight on water; if the enemy cuts the pontoon bridge, we will be attacked front and rear, and none will return!
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu was alarmed. He called his officers together and said, "Our army cannot fight on water. If the enemy cuts the pontoon bridge, we will be trapped between two forces and none of us will get home!

sentences.zh: 不如退守浮梁以待車駕。」

translations.literal: It would be better to withdraw and hold the pontoon bridge, awaiting the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: Better to fall back and hold the pontoon bridge until the emperor arrives."

sentences.zh: 上至圉鎮，聞其謀，亟遣中使乘驛止之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong reached Zhenzhen post, he heard of this plan and urgently dispatched a palace envoy by post relay to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong had reached Zhenzhen when he learned of the plan and at once sent a palace envoy by post relay to forbid it.

sentences.zh: 比至，已焚芻糧，退保正陽。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, they had already burned the fodder and grain and withdrawn to hold Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the messenger arrived, Li Gu's men had already burned their fodder and supplies and fallen back to defend Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 丁未，帝至陳州，亟遣李重進引兵趣淮上。

translations.literal: On day Dingwei, Emperor Shizong reached Chenzhou and urgently dispatched Li Chongjin to lead troops toward the Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: On day Dingwei Emperor Shizong reached Chenzhou and immediately ordered Li Chongjin to march toward the Huai.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，李穀奏：「賊艦中淮而進，弩砲所不能及，若浮梁不守，則眾心動搖，須至退軍。

translations.literal: On day Xinhai, Li Gu memorialized: "The enemy warships advance midstream on the Huai, beyond the reach of crossbows and catapults; if the pontoon bridge is not held, the troops' hearts will waver and withdrawal will become unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: On day Xinhai Li Gu submitted a memorial: "The enemy ships are pushing up the middle of the Huai, out of range of our crossbows and catapults. If we cannot hold the pontoon bridge, morale will collapse and we will have no choice but to retreat.

sentences.zh: 今賊艦日進，淮水日漲，若車駕親臨，萬一糧道阻絕，其危不測。

translations.literal: Now the enemy warships advance daily and the Huai rises daily; if Your Majesty comes in person, should the supply route be cut off, the danger cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fleet advances every day and the Huai rises every day. If Your Majesty comes in person and our supply line is cut, the danger is incalculable.

sentences.zh: 願陛下且駐蹕陳、穎，俟李重進至，臣與之共度賊艦可御，浮梁可完，立具奏聞。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would halt at Chen and Ying, wait until Li Chongjin arrives, and then I with him will together assess whether the enemy warships can be resisted and the pontoon bridge completed, and immediately report in full.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to halt at Chen and Ying until Li Chongjin arrives. He and I will then assess together whether the enemy ships can be countered and the pontoon bridge secured, and report at once.

sentences.zh: 但若厲兵秣馬，春去冬來，足使賊中疲弊，取之未晚。」

translations.literal: But if we only sharpen weapons and feed horses, from spring's passing to winter's return, that will suffice to wear down the enemy; taking them will not be late."
translations.idiomatic: If we simply keep our armies ready and wait from spring through winter, that alone will exhaust the enemy. There will still be time to take them."

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏，不悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor read the memorial and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong read the memorial and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 劉彥貞素驕貴，無才略，不習兵，所歷籓鎮，專為貪暴，積財巨億，以賂權要，由是魏岑等爭譽之，以為治民如龔、黃，用兵如韓、彭，故周師至，唐主首用之。

translations.literal: Liu Yanzhen had long been proud and honored, without talent or strategy, untrained in warfare; in every frontier command he had been devoted to greed and cruelty, amassing wealth in the hundreds of millions to bribe powerful men. From this Wei Cen and others vied to praise him, saying he governed the people like Gong Sui and Huang Ba and used troops like Han Xin and Peng Yue. Therefore when Zhou armies arrived, the Southern Tang ruler put him in command first.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanzhen had long enjoyed rank and privilege but possessed neither talent nor military skill. In every command he had served, he devoted himself to greed and cruelty, amassing wealth in the hundreds of millions to buy favor with the powerful. Wei Cen and others competed to praise him, claiming he governed like Gong Sui and Huang Ba and commanded armies like Han Xin and Peng Yue. When the Zhou armies arrived, the Southern Tang ruler made him his first choice.

sentences.zh: 其裨將咸師朗等皆勇而無謀，聞李穀退，喜，引兵直抵正陽，旌旗輜重數百里，劉仁贍及池州刺史張全約固止之。

translations.literal: His subordinate generals Xian Shilang and others were all brave but without strategy; hearing Li Gu had withdrawn, they rejoiced and led troops straight to Zhengyang, banners and baggage trains stretching for several hundred li. Liu Renshan and Chizhou prefect Zhang Quanyue firmly tried to stop them.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate generals, including Xian Shilang, were brave but rash. Learning that Li Gu had withdrawn, they were delighted and marched straight for Zhengyang, their banners and supply trains stretching for hundreds of li. Liu Renshan and Chizhou prefect Zhang Quanyue strongly urged them to stop.

sentences.zh: 仁贍曰：「公軍未至而敵人先遁，是畏公之威聲也，安用速戰！

translations.literal: Renshan said: "Before your army arrived the enemy already fled—this shows they fear your formidable reputation. Why rush to battle!
translations.idiomatic: Renshan said, "The enemy fled before your army even arrived—that shows they fear your reputation. Why force a quick battle?

sentences.zh: 萬一失利，則大事去矣！」

translations.literal: If by any chance we suffer defeat, the great enterprise will be lost!"
translations.idiomatic: If we lose even once, the whole campaign is finished!"

sentences.zh: 彥貞不從。

translations.literal: Yanzhen did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 既行，仁贍曰：「果遇，必敗。」

translations.literal: After he had set out, Renshan said: "If they truly meet, defeat is certain."
translations.idiomatic: After Yanzhen marched out, Renshan said, "If they meet the enemy, they are sure to be beaten."

sentences.zh: 乃益兵乘城為備。

translations.literal: He then added troops to man the walls in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: He then reinforced the garrison and prepared the city's defenses.

sentences.zh: 李重進度淮，逆戰於正陽東，大破之，斬彥貞，生擒咸師朗等，斬首萬餘級，伏屍三十里，收軍資器械三十餘萬。

translations.literal: Li Chongjin crossed the Huai and met them in battle east of Zhengyang, routing them completely; Yanzhen was beheaded, Xian Shilang and others were captured alive, more than ten thousand heads were taken, corpses lay for thirty li, and military stores and equipment numbering more than three hundred thousand items were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin crossed the Huai and met Liu Yanzhen east of Zhengyang, crushing his army. Yanzhen was killed in battle, Xian Shilang and others were captured alive, more than ten thousand heads were taken, the dead covered thirty li of ground, and more than three hundred thousand items of military stores and equipment were seized.

sentences.zh: 是時江、淮久安，民不習戰，彥貞既敗，唐人大恐，張全約收餘眾奔壽州，劉仁贍表全約為馬步左廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: At this time the Jiang and Huai regions had long known peace and the people were unused to war. After Yanzhen's defeat the people of Southern Tang were greatly terrified. Zhang Quanyue gathered the remnant troops and fled to Shouzhou; Liu Renshan memorialized to appoint Quanyue commander of the left wing of horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang and Huai regions had long been at peace, and the people were unused to war. After Yanzhen's defeat Southern Tang was gripped by terror. Zhang Quanyue gathered the survivors and fled to Shouzhou, and Liu Renshan recommended him as commander of the left wing of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 皇甫暉、姚鳳退保清流關。

translations.literal: Huangfu Hui and Yao Feng withdrew to hold Qingliu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui and Yao Feng fell back to defend Qingliu Pass.

sentences.zh: 滁州刺史王紹顏委城走。

translations.literal: Chuzhou prefect Wang Shaoyan abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhou prefect Wang Shaoyan abandoned his post and fled.

sentences.zh: 壬子，帝至永寧鎮，謂侍臣曰：「聞壽州圍解，農民多歸村落，今聞大軍至，必復入城。

translations.literal: On day Renzi, Emperor Shizong reached Yongning post and said to his attending ministers: "I hear that since the siege of Shouzhou was lifted, many farmers have returned to their villages. Now that they hear the great army is coming, they will surely enter the cities again.
translations.idiomatic: On day Renzi Emperor Shizong reached Yongning and told his ministers, "When the siege of Shouzhou was lifted, many farmers returned to their villages. Now that they hear our army is coming, they will surely flee back into the cities.

sentences.zh: 憐其聚為餓殍，宜先遣使存撫，各令安業。」

translations.literal: Pitying that they may gather and become corpses of starvation, we should first dispatch envoys to comfort and reassure them, each being ordered to settle to their livelihoods."
translations.idiomatic: I pity them—they may crowd together and starve. We should send envoys ahead to reassure them and let each household return to its work in peace."

sentences.zh: 甲寅，帝至正陽，以李重進代李穀為淮南道行營都招討使，以穀判壽州行府事。

translations.literal: On day Jiayin, Emperor Shizong reached Zhengyang, made Li Chongjin replace Li Gu as overall commander and commander-in-chief of the Huainan route field headquarters, and made Gu administer Shouzhou field headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On day Jiayin Emperor Shizong reached Zhengyang. He replaced Li Gu with Li Chongjin as overall commander of the Huainan campaign and put Li Gu in charge of affairs at the Shouzhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，帝至壽州城下，營於淝水之陽，命諸軍圍壽州，徙正陽浮梁於下蔡鎮。

translations.literal: On day Bingchen, Emperor Shizong reached beneath the walls of Shouzhou, encamped on the south bank of the Fei River, ordered the various armies to besiege Shouzhou, and moved the Zhengyang pontoon bridge to Xiaxia post.
translations.idiomatic: On day Bingchen Emperor Shizong reached Shouzhou and encamped on the south bank of the Fei. He ordered all armies to invest the city and had the Zhengyang pontoon bridge relocated to Xiaxia.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，征宋、毫、陳、穎、徐、宿、許、蔡等州丁夫數十萬以攻城，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: On day Dingsi, he conscripted several hundred thousand corvée laborers from Song, Bo, Chen, Ying, Xu, Su, Xu, and Cai prefectures to assault the city, without rest day or night.
translations.idiomatic: On day Dingsi he conscripted several hundred thousand laborers from Song, Bo, Chen, Ying, Xu, Su, Xu, and Cai to press the siege, working without pause day or night.

sentences.zh: 唐兵萬餘人維舟於淮，營於塗山之下。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand Southern Tang troops moored their boats on the Huai and encamped below Mount Tu.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand Southern Tang troops anchored their ships on the Huai and encamped below Mount Tu.

sentences.zh: 庚申，帝命太祖皇帝擊之，太祖皇帝遣百餘騎薄其營而偽遁，伏兵邀之，大敗唐兵於渦口，斬其都監何延錫等，奪戰艦五十餘艘。

translations.literal: On day Gengshen, Emperor Shizong ordered Zhao Kuangyin—the palace guard commander whom Sima Guang retrospectively styles Emperor Taizu—to attack them. Zhao Kuangyin sent more than a hundred horsemen to press close to their camp and then feign retreat; ambush troops intercepted them and routed Southern Tang forces at Wokou, beheading their chief inspector He Yanxi and others and seizing more than fifty warships.
translations.idiomatic: On day Gengshen Emperor Shizong ordered Zhao Kuangyin, the palace guard commander whom Sima Guang retrospectively styles Emperor Taizu, to attack them. Zhao Kuangyin sent a little over a hundred horsemen to ride up to the enemy camp and then feign retreat. His ambush force cut them off and routed the Southern Tang army at Wokou, killing chief inspector He Yanxi and others and capturing more than fifty warships.

sentences.zh: 詔以武平節度使兼中書令王逵為南面行營都統，使攻唐之鄂州。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Wuping military governor and concurrent Grand Censor Wang Kui overall commander of the southern route field headquarters, ordering him to attack Southern Tang's Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Wuping military governor and concurrent Grand Censor Wang Kui overall commander of the southern campaign and ordered him to attack Southern Tang's Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 逵引兵過岳州，岳州團練使潘叔嗣厚具燕犒，奉事甚謹。

translations.literal: Kui led troops through Yuezhou; Yuezhou regimental commissioner Pan Shusi lavishly prepared feasts and rewards and served him with great deference.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui marched through Yuezhou, where regimental commissioner Pan Shusi entertained him lavishly and waited on him with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 逵左右求取無厭，不滿望者譖叔嗣於逵，雲其謀叛，逵怒形於詞色，叔嗣由是懼不自安。

translations.literal: Kui's attendants demanded without satiety; those whose expectations were not met slandered Shusi to Kui, saying he plotted rebellion. Kui's anger showed in word and countenance, and Shusi from this feared and was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui's attendants demanded gifts without end. Those who felt shortchanged slandered Pan Shusi to Wang Kui, claiming he was plotting rebellion. Wang Kui's anger showed plainly in his words and face, and Pan Shusi grew fearful and uneasy.

sentences.zh: 唐主聞湖南兵將至，命武昌節度使何敬洙徙民入城，為固守之計。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler heard that Hunan troops were about to arrive and ordered Wuchang military governor He Jingzhu to move the people into the city as a plan for firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Hunan troops were approaching, the Southern Tang ruler ordered Wuchang military governor He Jingzhu to move the populace inside the walls and prepare for a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 敬洙不從，使除地為戰場，曰：「敵至，則與兵民俱死於此耳！」

translations.literal: Jingzhu did not follow the order; he had ground cleared for a battlefield and said: "When the enemy arrives, then soldiers and people alike will die here!"
translations.idiomatic: He Jingzhu refused. He cleared ground for a battlefield and said, "When the enemy comes, soldiers and civilians alike will die here together!"

sentences.zh: 唐主善之。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙寅，下蔡浮梁成，上自往視之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on day Bingyin, the Xiaxia pontoon bridge was completed; Emperor Shizong went in person to inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on day Bingyin, the pontoon bridge at Xiaxia was finished, and Emperor Shizong went to inspect it in person.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，廬、拜、光、黃巡檢使元城司超奏敗唐兵三千餘人於盛唐，擒都監高弼等，獲戰艦四十餘艘。

translations.literal: On day Wuchen, Si Chao, patrol commissioner of Luzhou, Haozhou, Guangzhou, and Huangzhou from Yuancheng, memorialized that he had defeated more than three thousand Southern Tang troops at Sheng Tang, captured chief inspector Gao Bi and others, and seized more than forty warships.
translations.idiomatic: On day Wuchen Si Chao, patrol commissioner for Luzhou, Haozhou, Guangzhou, and Huangzhou, reported a victory over more than three thousand Southern Tang troops at Sheng Tang. He captured chief inspector Gao Bi and others and took more than forty warships.

sentences.zh: 上命太祖皇帝倍道襲清流關。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong ordered Zhao Kuangyin to march by double stages and strike Qingliu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong ordered Zhao Kuangyin to force-march and strike Qingliu Pass.

sentences.zh: 皇甫暉等陳於山下，方與前鋒戰，太祖皇帝引兵出山後；

translations.literal: Huangfu Hui and others drew up in formation below the mountain and were just engaging the vanguard when Zhao Kuangyin led troops out from behind the mountain;
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui and his men formed up below the mountain and were fighting the vanguard when Zhao Kuangyin led his troops out from behind the peak;

sentences.zh: 暉等大驚，走入滁州，欲斷橋自守。

translations.literal: Hui and the others were greatly alarmed, fled into Chuzhou, and wished to break the bridge and hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui and his men were thrown into panic, fled into Chuzhou, and tried to destroy the bridge and hold the city.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝躍馬麾兵涉水，直抵城下。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangyin spurred his horse, waved his troops forward, crossed the water, and pressed straight to the foot of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin spurred his horse forward, led his men through the water, and rode straight to the city wall.

sentences.zh: 暉曰：「人各為其主，願容成列而戰。」

translations.literal: Hui said: "Each man serves his own lord; I ask that we be allowed to form ranks and fight."
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui said, "Every man serves his own master. Grant us leave to form ranks and fight."

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝笑而許之。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangyin smiled and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin smiled and agreed.

sentences.zh: 暉整眾而出，太祖皇帝擁馬頸突陳而入，大呼曰：「吾止取皇甫暉，他人非吾敵也！」

translations.literal: Hui marshaled his troops and came out; Zhao Kuangyin seized his horse's neck and burst through the formation, shouting loudly: "I seek only Huangfu Hui—the rest of you are not my match!"
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui drew up his men and came out. Zhao Kuangyin gathered his horse's reins and charged straight through the ranks, shouting, "I want only Huangfu Hui—the rest of you are no match for me!"

sentences.zh: 手劍擊暉，中腦，生擒之，並擒姚鳳，遂克滁州。

translations.literal: With his hand sword he struck Hui, hitting his head; he captured him alive, also captured Yao Feng, and then took Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Huangfu Hui with his sword and hit him in the head, then took him alive along with Yao Feng and captured Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 後數日，宣祖皇帝為馬軍副都指揮使，引兵夜半至滁州城下，傳呼開門。

translations.literal: Several days later Zhao Hongyin—whom Sima Guang retrospectively styles Patriarch Xuannzu—serving as deputy commander of the horse army, led troops at midnight to beneath the walls of Chuzhou and called out to have the gate opened.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Zhao Hongyin, Zhao Kuangyin's father whom Sima Guang retrospectively styles Patriarch Xuannzu and who was then deputy commander of the horse army, brought troops to Chuzhou in the middle of the night and called for the gate to be opened.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝曰：「父子雖至親，城門王事也，不敢奉命！」

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangyin said: "Though father and son are closest kin, the city gate is the king's business—I dare not obey the command!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin said, "Father and son may be closest of kin, but the city gate is the king's business. I dare not obey!"

sentences.zh: 明旦，乃得入。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, he was only then admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Only at dawn the next day was he admitted.

sentences.zh: 上遣翰林學士竇儀籍滁州帑藏，太祖皇帝遣親吏取藏中絹。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong dispatched Hanlin academician Dou Yi to register Chuzhou's treasury stores; Zhao Kuangyin sent a personal clerk to take silk from the stores.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong sent Hanlin academician Dou Yi to inventory Chuzhou's treasury, but Zhao Kuangyin sent a personal clerk to take silk from the stores.

sentences.zh: 儀曰：「公初克城時，雖傾藏取之，無傷也。

translations.literal: Yi said: "When you first took the city, even if you emptied the stores and took all, no harm would be done.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi said, "When you first captured the city, you could have emptied the stores without blame.

sentences.zh: 今既籍為官物，非有詔書，不可得也。」

translations.literal: Now that they have been registered as government property, without an edict they cannot be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: But now that they have been registered as government property, you cannot take them without an imperial edict."

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝由是重儀。

translations.literal: From this Zhao Kuangyin came to respect Yi.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Zhao Kuangyin held Dou Yi in high regard.

sentences.zh: 詔左金吾衛將軍馬崇祚知滁州。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Left Golden Guard general Ma Chongzuo to administer Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Left Golden Guard general Ma Chongzuo prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，永興節度使劉詞遺表薦其幕僚薊人趙普有才可用。

translations.literal: Initially, Yongxing military governor Liu Ci in a death memorial recommended his staff officer Zhao Pu of Ji as talented and usable.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on his deathbed Yongxing military governor Liu Ci had recommended his staff officer Zhao Pu of Ji as a man of talent worth employing.

sentences.zh: 會滁州平，范質薦普為滁州軍事判官，太祖皇帝與語，悅之。

translations.literal: When Chuzhou was pacified, Fan Zhi recommended Pu as Chuzhou military adjutant; Zhao Kuangyin conversed with him and was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuzhou fell, Fan Zhi recommended Zhao Pu as military adjutant of Chuzhou. Zhao Kuangyin spoke with him and was impressed.

sentences.zh: 時獲盜百餘人，皆應死，普請先訊鞫然後決，所活什七八。

translations.literal: At the time more than a hundred bandits were captured, all deserving death; Pu requested that they first be interrogated and tried and then sentenced, and seven or eight tenths of them were spared.
translations.idiomatic: At the time more than a hundred captured bandits all faced the death penalty. Zhao Pu asked that they be interrogated before judgment, and seven or eight out of ten were spared.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝益奇之。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangyin regarded him all the more as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝威名日盛，每臨陳，必以繁纓飾馬，鎧仗鮮明。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangyin's formidable reputation daily grew; whenever he faced battle he always adorned his horse with an ornate tassel and kept armor and weapons bright and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin's fame grew daily. Whenever he took the field he adorned his horse with an ornate tassel and wore armor and weapons of striking brilliance.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「如此，為敵所識。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "In this way you will be recognized by the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Dress like that and the enemy will recognize you at once."

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝曰：「吾固欲其識之耳！」

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangyin said: "I precisely want them to recognize me!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin replied, "That is exactly what I want!"

sentences.zh: 唐主遣泗州牙將王知朗繼書抵徐州，稱：「唐皇帝奉書大周皇帝，請息兵修好，願以兄事帝，歲輸貨財以助軍費。」

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler dispatched Sizhou gate officer Wang Zhilang with successive letters reaching Xuzhou, stating: "The Tang Emperor presents a letter to the Great Zhou Emperor, requesting a ceasefire and restored friendship, wishing to treat the Emperor as an elder brother, and annually delivering goods and wealth to assist military expenses."
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler sent Sizhou gate officer Wang Zhilang with a letter to Xuzhou, saying, "The Tang emperor writes to the emperor of Great Zhou to ask for peace. He is willing to treat Emperor Shizong as an elder brother and pay tribute each year to help defray military costs."

sentences.zh: 甲戌，徐州以聞；

translations.literal: On day Jiaxu, Xuzhou reported this;
translations.idiomatic: On day Jiaxu Xuzhou forwarded the letter;

sentences.zh: 帝不答。

translations.literal: the Emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong made no reply.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，命前武勝節度使侯章等攻壽州水寨，決其壕之西北隅，導壕水入於淝。

translations.literal: On day Wuyin, he ordered former Wusheng military governor Hou Zhang and others to attack Shouzhou's water fort, breach the northwest corner of its moat, and channel the moat water into the Fei.
translations.idiomatic: On day Wuyin he ordered former Wusheng military governor Hou Zhang and others to attack Shouzhou's river fort, breach the northwest corner of the moat, and divert the water into the Fei.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝遣使獻皇甫暉等，暉傷甚，見上，臥而言曰：「臣非不忠於所事，但士卒勇怯不同耳。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangyin sent envoys to present Huangfu Hui and others; Hui was badly wounded. Seeing Emperor Shizong, he spoke lying down, saying: "Your subject is not disloyal to the lord he served, but soldiers differ in courage and timidity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangyin sent Huangfu Hui and the other captives to the emperor. Badly wounded, Huangfu Hui was brought before Emperor Shizong and spoke from his couch: "I was not disloyal to my master. It is only that some soldiers are brave and others are not.

sentences.zh: 臣曏日屢與契丹戰，未嘗見兵精如此。」

translations.literal: Your subject in former days repeatedly fought the Khitan and never saw troops as elite as these."
translations.idiomatic: I have fought the Khitan many times, and I have never seen troops as fine as yours."

sentences.zh: 因盛稱太祖皇帝之勇。

translations.literal: He then lavishly praised Zhao Kuangyin's bravery.
translations.idiomatic: He then spoke at length of Zhao Kuangyin's valor.

sentences.zh: 上釋之，後數日卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong released him; several days later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong set him free, but he died a few days later.

sentences.zh: 帝詗知揚州無備，己卯，命韓令坤等將兵襲之，戒以毋得殘民；

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong learned by inquiry that Yangzhou was undefended. On day Jimao he ordered Han Lingkun and others to lead troops in a surprise attack on it, admonishing them that the people must not be harmed;
translations.idiomatic: Learning through scouts that Yangzhou was undefended, Emperor Shizong on day Jimao ordered Han Lingkun and others to strike it by surprise, warning them not to harm the populace;

sentences.zh: 其李氏陵寢，遣人與李氏人共守護之。

translations.literal: as for the tombs of the Li clan, he dispatched men to guard them together with members of the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: and he sent men to guard the Li clan tombs together with members of the Li family.

sentences.zh: 唐主兵屢敗，懼亡，乃遣翰林學士、戶部侍郎鐘謨、工部侍郎、文理院學士李德明奉表稱臣，來請平，獻御服、茶藥及金器千兩，銀器五千兩，繒錦二千匹，犒軍牛五百頭，酒二千斛，壬午，至壽州城下。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler's armies had repeatedly been defeated and he feared destruction; he then dispatched Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Zhong Mo and Vice Minister of Works and Wenli Academy academician Li Deming bearing a memorial declaring himself subject, coming to sue for peace, presenting imperial robes, tea and medicines, one thousand liang of gold vessels, five thousand liang of silver vessels, two thousand bolts of silk brocade, five hundred oxen to reward the army, and two thousand hu of wine. On day Renwu they reached beneath the walls of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats the Southern Tang ruler feared for his state's survival. He sent Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Zhong Mo and Vice Minister of Works and Wenli Academy academician Li Deming with a memorial submitting as a vassal and suing for peace. They brought imperial robes, tea and medicines, a thousand liang of gold vessels, five thousand liang of silver vessels, two thousand bolts of silk brocade, five hundred oxen to reward the army, and two thousand hu of wine. On day Renwu they arrived below Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 謨、德明素辯口，上知其欲遊說，盛陳甲兵而見之，曰：「爾主自謂唐室苗裔，宜知禮義，異於他國。

translations.literal: Mo and Deming were by nature skilled in debate; Emperor Shizong knew they wished to persuade and received them with armor and troops arrayed in strength, saying: "Your lord calls himself a descendant of the Tang house and ought to know ritual and righteousness, different from other states.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Mo and Li Deming were both gifted speakers. Emperor Shizong knew they had come to negotiate and received them amid a display of armed troops. He said, "Your master claims descent from the Tang house and ought to know ritual and righteousness better than other states.

sentences.zh: 與朕止隔一水，未嘗遣一介修好，惟泛海通契丹，捨華事夷，禮義安在？

translations.literal: He is separated from Us by only one river, yet never sent a single envoy to restore friendship, only sending letters by sea to reach the Khitan, abandoning China to serve barbarians—where is ritual and righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: He is separated from me by only one river, yet never sent a single envoy to keep the peace. Instead he sent messages by sea to the Khitan, abandoning China to serve barbarians—where is the ritual and righteousness in that?

sentences.zh: 且汝欲說我令罷兵邪？

translations.literal: Moreover, do you wish to persuade Me to halt the armies?
translations.idiomatic: And do you mean to talk me into halting the campaign?

sentences.zh: 我非六國愚主，豈汝口舌所能移邪！

translations.literal: I am not a foolish ruler of the Six States—can your tongues move Me!
translations.idiomatic: I am no foolish ruler of the Warring States era. Do you think your tongues can move me?

sentences.zh: 可歸語汝主：亟來見朕，再拜謝過，則無事矣。

translations.literal: You may return and tell your lord: come quickly to see Us, bow twice and confess fault, and then there will be no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Go back and tell your master to come at once, bow before me twice, and confess his fault—then there will be no further trouble.

sentences.zh: 不然，朕欲觀金陵城，借府庫以勞軍，汝君臣得無悔乎！」

translations.literal: Otherwise, We wish to view Jinling city and borrow the treasury to reward the army—will you lord and ministers not regret it!"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I mean to see Jinling for myself and use your treasury to reward my army. Will you and your master not regret that?"

sentences.zh: 謨、德明戰慄不敢言。

translations.literal: Mo and Deming trembled with fear and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Mo and Li Deming trembled and dared not answer.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘俶遣兵屯境上以俟周命。

translations.literal: Wuyue king Qian Hongchu dispatched troops to encamp on the border to await Zhou orders.
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Hongchu of Wuyue posted troops on the border to await orders from Zhou.

sentences.zh: 蘇州營田指揮使陳滿言於丞相吳程曰：「周師南征，唐舉國驚擾，常州無備，易取也。」

translations.literal: Suzhou camp-field commander Chen Man spoke to chief minister Wu Cheng, saying: "Zhou armies campaign south; Southern Tang is alarmed throughout the realm; Changzhou is undefended and easy to take."
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou camp-field commander Chen Man told chief minister Wu Cheng, "The Zhou armies are campaigning south, Southern Tang is in turmoil, and Changzhou is undefended—it can be taken easily."

sentences.zh: 會唐主有詔撫安江陰吏民，滿告程云：「周詔書已至。」

translations.literal: It happened that the Southern Tang ruler had an edict to reassure the officials and people of Jiangyin; Man told Cheng, saying: "The Zhou edict has already arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Southern Tang ruler issued an edict to reassure the officials and people of Jiangyin. Chen Man told Wu Cheng, "The Zhou edict has already reached there."

sentences.zh: 程為之言於弘俶，請亟發兵從其策。

translations.literal: Cheng spoke of this to Hongchu on his behalf and requested that troops be sent urgently to follow this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cheng relayed this to Qian Hongchu and urged him to send troops at once and adopt the plan.

sentences.zh: 丞相元德昭曰：「唐大國，未可輕也。

translations.literal: Chief minister Yuan Dezhao said: "Southern Tang is a great state and must not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Yuan Dezhao said, "Southern Tang is a great power and must not be underestimated.

sentences.zh: 若我入唐境而周師不至，誰與並力，能無危乎！

translations.literal: If we enter Southern Tang territory while Zhou armies do not arrive, with whom shall we join forces—can we be without danger!
translations.idiomatic: If we enter Southern Tang territory and the Zhou armies fail to come, with whom will we join forces? How can we avoid disaster?

sentences.zh: 請姑俟之。」

translations.literal: I request that we wait for the time being."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that we wait a little longer."

sentences.zh: 程固爭，以為時不可失，弘俶卒從程議。

translations.literal: Cheng firmly contended, holding that the moment must not be lost; Hongchu finally followed Cheng's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cheng argued fiercely that the moment must not be lost, and Qian Hongchu finally accepted his plan.

sentences.zh: 癸未，遣程督衢州刺史鮑修讓、中直都指揮使羅晟趣常州。

translations.literal: On day Guiwei, he dispatched Cheng to supervise Quzhou prefect Bao Xiurang and Central Direct commander Luo Sheng in pressing toward Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On day Guiwei he sent Wu Cheng to lead Quzhou prefect Bao Xiurang and Central Direct commander Luo Sheng in a rapid march on Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 程謂將士曰：「元丞相不欲出師。」

translations.literal: Cheng said to the officers and soldiers: "Chief Minister Yuan did not wish to send out the army."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cheng told the troops, "Chief Minister Yuan did not want us to march."

sentences.zh: 將士怒，流言欲擊德昭。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers were angry; rumors spread that they wished to strike Dezhao.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were furious, and word spread that they meant to attack Yuan Dezhao.

sentences.zh: 弘俶匿德昭於府中，令捕言者，歎曰：「方出師而士卒欲擊丞相，不祥甚哉！」

translations.literal: Hongchu hid Dezhao in the palace compound, ordered the arrest of those who spoke thus, and sighed, saying: "Just as the army is setting out the soldiers wish to strike the chief minister—how very inauspicious!"
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hongchu hid Yuan Dezhao in the palace, ordered the rumor-mongers arrested, and sighed, "We are just setting out on campaign and already the soldiers want to attack the chief minister—what an ill omen!"

sentences.zh: 乙酉，韓令坤奄至揚州。

translations.literal: On day Yiyou, Han Lingkun suddenly arrived at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On day Yiyou Han Lingkun suddenly appeared at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 平旦，先遣白延遇以數百騎馳入城，城中不之覺。

translations.literal: At dawn he first dispatched Bai Yanyu with several hundred horsemen to gallop into the city; the city did not notice them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he first sent Bai Yanyu with several hundred horsemen galloping into the city before anyone inside knew what was happening.

sentences.zh: 令坤繼至，唐東都營屯使賈崇焚官府民舍，棄城南走，副留守工部侍郎馮延魯髡發被僧服，匿於佛寺，軍士執之。

translations.literal: Lingkun followed and arrived; Southern Tang eastern capital camp garrison commissioner Jia Chong burned government offices and private houses and abandoned the city fleeing south; deputy regent and Vice Minister of Works Feng Yanlu shaved his head, wore monk's robes, and hid in a Buddhist temple; soldiers seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun arrived next. Southern Tang eastern capital camp commissioner Jia Chong burned the government offices and private houses and fled south. Deputy regent and Vice Minister of Works Feng Yanlu shaved his head, put on monk's robes, and hid in a temple, but soldiers captured him.

sentences.zh: 令坤慰撫其民，使皆安堵。

translations.literal: Lingkun comforted and reassured the people, causing all to settle in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun reassured the populace and restored order.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，王逵奏拔鄂州長山寨，執其將陳澤等，獻之。

translations.literal: On day Gengyin, Wang Kui memorialized that he had taken Changshan stockade of Ezhou, captured its generals Chen Ze and others, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On day Gengyin Wang Kui reported the capture of Changshan stockade in Ezhou and the seizure of its generals Chen Ze and others, whom he sent as captives.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，太祖皇帝奏唐天長制置使耿謙降，獲芻糧二十餘萬。

translations.literal: On day Xinmao, Zhao Kuangyin memorialized that Southern Tang Tianchang commissioner Geng Qian had surrendered and more than two hundred thousand units of fodder and grain were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: On day Xinmao Zhao Kuangyin reported that Southern Tang Tianchang commissioner Geng Qian had surrendered and that more than two hundred thousand units of fodder and grain were captured.

sentences.zh: 唐主遣園苑使尹延范如泰州，遷吳讓皇之族於潤州。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler dispatched garden-park commissioner Yin Yanfan to Taizhou to relocate the clan of the abdicated Wu emperor to Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler sent garden commissioner Yin Yanfan to Taizhou to move the abdicated Wu emperor's clan to Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 延范以道路艱難，恐楊氏為變，盡殺其男子六十人，還報，唐主怒，腰斬之。

translations.literal: Yanfan, because the roads were difficult, feared the Yang clan might rebel; he killed all sixty of their men, returned and reported, and the Southern Tang ruler in anger had him cut in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yanfan feared the Yang clan might rebel on the difficult road and killed all sixty of their men. When he reported back, the Southern Tang ruler was furious and had him cut in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 韓令坤攻唐泰州，拔之，刺史方訥奔金陵。

translations.literal: Han Lingkun attacked Southern Tang's Taizhou, took it, and prefect Fang Ne fled to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun attacked Southern Tang's Taizhou, captured it, and prefect Fang Ne fled to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 唐主遣人以蠟丸求救於契丹。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler dispatched men with wax-sealed messages to seek rescue from the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler sent men with wax-sealed messages to beg the Khitan for help.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，靜安軍使何繼先獲而獻之。

translations.literal: On day Renchen, He Jixian, commissioner of the Jing'an Army, captured it and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On day Renchen, Jing'an Army commissioner He Jixian captured the wax-sealed message and presented it to the court.

sentences.zh: 以給事中高防權知泰州。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Gao Fang was made acting prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Gao Fang was appointed acting prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，吳越王弘俶遣上直都指揮使路彥銖攻宣州，羅晟帥戰艦屯江陰。

translations.literal: On day Guisi, Qian Hongchu, King of Wuyue, sent the commander of the inner guard, Lu Yanzhen, to attack Xuanzhou; Luo Sheng led warships to encamp at Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: On day Guisi, Wuyue king Qian Hongchu sent inner-guard commander Lu Yanzhen against Xuanzhou while Luo Sheng anchored the fleet at Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 唐靜海制置使姚彥洪帥兵民萬人奔吳越。

translations.literal: Yao Yanhong, commissioner of Jinghai for Tang, led ten thousand soldiers and civilians in flight to Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang's Jinghai commissioner Yao Yanhong fled to Wuyue with ten thousand troops and civilians.

sentences.zh: 潘叔嗣屬將士而告之曰：「吾事令公至矣，今乃信讒疑怒，軍還，必擊我。

translations.literal: Pan Shusi assembled the officers and soldiers and told them: "I have served the Lord to the utmost; now he believes slander, grows suspicious and angry—when the army returns, he will surely strike me.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Shusi gathered his officers and men and said, "I have served Lord Wang to the limit of loyalty. Now he believes slanders against me and is furious—when his army returns, he will surely destroy me.

sentences.zh: 吾不能坐而待死，汝輩能與我俱西乎？」

translations.literal: I cannot sit and await death—can you gentlemen march west with me?"
translations.idiomatic: I will not sit here and wait to die. Will you march west with me?"

sentences.zh: 眾憤怒，請行，叔嗣帥之西襲朗州。

translations.literal: The multitude, enraged, requested to march; Shusi led them west in a surprise attack on Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The men, furious, demanded action, and Shusi led them west in a surprise strike on Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 逵聞之，還軍追之，及於武陵城外，與叔嗣戰，逵敗死，或勸叔嗣遂據朗州，叔嗣曰：「吾救死耳，安敢自尊？

translations.literal: Kui heard of it, turned his army back in pursuit, caught up outside Wuling city, and fought Shusi; Kui was defeated and died. Some urged Shusi to seize Langzhou at once; Shusi said: "I sought only to save my life—how would I dare exalt myself?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kui turned back in pursuit and met Shusi outside Wuling. Kui was defeated and killed. Some urged Shusi to hold Langzhou, but he said, "I acted only to save my life—how dare I set myself up as a lord?

sentences.zh: 宜以督府歸潭州太尉，豈不以武安見處乎！」

translations.literal: The command post ought to be returned to the Grand Marshal of Tanzhou—would he not treat me with the Wu'an command!"
translations.idiomatic: The command should go back to the Grand Marshal at Tanzhou—surely he will reward me with the Wu'an post!"

sentences.zh: 乃歸岳州，使團練判官李簡帥朗州將吏迎武安節度使周行逢。

translations.literal: He then returned to Yuezhou and had regimental adjutant Li Jian lead Langzhou's officers and officials to welcome Zhou Xingfeng, military governor of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Yuezhou and sent regimental adjutant Li Jian with Langzhou's officials to welcome Wu'an military governor Zhou Xingfeng.

sentences.zh: 眾謂行逢：「必以潭州授叔嗣。」

translations.literal: The multitude told Xingfeng: "You must grant Tanzhou to Shusi."
translations.idiomatic: His advisers told Xingfeng, "You must give Tanzhou to Shusi."

sentences.zh: 行逢曰：「叔嗣賊殺主帥，罪當族。

translations.literal: Xingfeng said: "Shusi, as a traitor, killed his commander-in-chief—the crime warrants extermination of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng said, "Shusi murdered his commander—the crime warrants the extermination of his clan.

sentences.zh: 所可恕者，得武陵而不有，以授吾耳。

translations.literal: What may be forgiven is that he took Wuling yet did not keep it, but handed it to me.
translations.idiomatic: The one thing in his favor is that he took Wuling but did not keep it—he handed it to me.

sentences.zh: 若遽用為節度使，天下謂我與之同謀，何以自明！

translations.literal: If I promptly appoint him military governor, the realm will say I plotted with him—how can I clear myself!
translations.idiomatic: If I made him military governor at once, the world would say we had plotted together—how could I clear my name?

sentences.zh: 宜且以為行軍司馬，俟逾年，授以節鉞可也。」

translations.literal: For now he should be made campaigning marshal; after more than a year, investiture with the command baton will do."
translations.idiomatic: For now make him campaigning marshal; after a year or more, the full commission would be fitting."

sentences.zh: 乃以衡州刺史莫弘萬權知潭州，帥眾入朗州，自稱武平、武安留後，告於朝廷，以叔嗣為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He then had Hengzhou prefect Mo Hongwan act as prefect of Tanzhou, led his forces into Langzhou, styled himself acting governor of Wuping and Wu'an, reported to court, and appointed Shusi campaigning marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He put Hengzhou prefect Mo Hongwan in charge of Tanzhou, marched into Langzhou, styled himself acting governor of Wuping and Wu'an, reported to court, and named Shusi campaigning marshal.

sentences.zh: 叔嗣怒，稱疾不至。

translations.literal: Shusi, angry, claimed illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Shusi, furious, pleaded illness and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 行逢曰：「行軍司馬，吾嘗為之，權與節度使相埒耳，叔嗣猶不滿望，更欲圖我邪！」

translations.literal: Xingfeng said: "Campaigning marshal—I once held that post; its authority rivals a military governor's—yet Shusi is still not satisfied and wishes to plot against me!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng said, "I once held the post of campaigning marshal myself—its authority rivals that of a military governor. Shusi is still not satisfied—does he mean to plot against me?"

sentences.zh: 或說行逢：「授叔嗣武安節鉞以誘之，令至都府受命，此乃機上肉耳！」

translations.literal: Someone advised Xingfeng: "Grant Shusi the Wu'an command baton to lure him—order him to come to headquarters to receive appointment; he will be meat on the chopping block!"
translations.idiomatic: An adviser said, "Offer him the Wu'an commission to lure him in—summon him to headquarters to take office, and he will be meat on the block!"

sentences.zh: 行逢從之。

translations.literal: Xingfeng followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng agreed.

sentences.zh: 叔嗣將行，其所親止之，叔嗣自恃素以兄事行逢，相親善，遂行不疑。

translations.literal: As Shusi was about to depart, those close to him tried to stop him; Shusi relied on having always treated Xingfeng as an elder brother and on their mutual closeness, and so set out without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: As Shusi prepared to leave, his intimates tried to stop him, but he trusted the old bond—he had always treated Xingfeng as an elder brother—and went without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 行逢遣使迎候，道路相望，既至，自出效勞，相見甚歡。

translations.literal: Xingfeng sent envoys to welcome him along the road, one party meeting the next; once he arrived, Xingfeng came out himself to offer labor and greetings—they met in great joy.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng sent escorts to meet him all along the road. When Shusi arrived, Xingfeng came out in person to welcome him, and their meeting seemed full of warmth.

sentences.zh: 叔嗣入謁，未至聽事，遣人執之，立於庭下，責之曰：「汝為小校無大功，王逵用汝為團練使，一旦反殺主帥。

translations.literal: Shusi entered to pay respects; before he reached the audience hall, men were sent to seize him and stand him in the courtyard below. Xingfeng rebuked him: "You were a petty officer without great merit; Wang Kui made you regimental commissioner, yet in a single day you turned traitor and killed your commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shusi came in to pay his respects. Before he reached the audience hall, Xingfeng's men seized him and stood him in the courtyard. Xingfeng rebuked him: "You were a minor officer without great merit when Wang Kui made you regimental commissioner—and you repaid him by murdering your commander.

sentences.zh: 吾以疇昔之情，未忍斬汝，以為行軍司馬，乃敢違拒吾命而不受乎！」

translations.literal: Out of our old friendship I could not bear to behead you and made you campaigning marshal—yet you dared defy my order and refuse to accept!"
translations.idiomatic: Out of old friendship I spared your life and made you campaigning marshal—and you dared defy my orders and refuse to come!"

sentences.zh: 叔嗣知不免，以宗族為請。

translations.literal: Shusi knew he could not escape and begged for his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shusi knew his end had come and begged only for his clan.

sentences.zh: 遂斬之。

translations.literal: He was then beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Xingfeng had him beheaded.
